name: GNSS positioning
summary: GPS, Galileo, GLONASS, BeiDou, QZSS, NavIC: signals, receivers, positioning.

name: RTK / PPP precise positioning

name: Software-defined GNSS receivers

name: Jamming and spoofing

name: Assured / resilient PNT

name: Timing and time transfer

name: Inertial navigation (INS/IMU)
summary: Strapdown mechanization, IMU error models, calibration, dead reckoning.

name: Sensor fusion and state estimation
summary: Kalman filters (EKF/UKF/ESKF/IEKF), factor graphs, smoothing, multi-sensor integration.

name: GNSS/INS integration
summary: Loosely, tightly and deeply coupled GNSS/INS.

name: Sensor calibration
summary: Camera-IMU, LiDAR-IMU extrinsics, intrinsics, time offset, Allan variance.

name: Visual(-inertial) odometry
summary: VO/VIO from monocular, stereo, event cameras with IMU.

name: Visual SLAM

name: LiDAR odometry and SLAM
summary: LiDAR(-inertial) odometry, scan matching, LiDAR mapping.

name: Radar navigation and odometry
summary: Radar odometry, radar SLAM, radar altimeters, Doppler velocity.

name: Place recognition and loop closure

name: Feature detection and matching
summary: Keypoints/descriptors and learned matchers (SIFT, SuperPoint, LightGlue, LoFTR).

name: Visual geo-localization (image-to-map)
summary: Matching UAV/ground imagery to satellite orthophotos or maps for absolute position without GNSS.

name: Terrain-relative navigation
summary: TERCOM/TRN/DSMAC-style matching of altimetry or imagery against DEM/terrain databases.

name: Magnetic anomaly navigation

name: Celestial and star-tracker navigation
summary: Star trackers, sun/sky polarization, celestial fixes.

name: Signals of opportunity
summary: Positioning from LTE/5G, Wi-Fi, DVB, LEO satellites (Starlink, Iridium), eLoran, other non-navigation RF.

name: RF localization and direction finding
summary: UWB, TDOA/AOA, direction finding, emitter geolocation, beacons.

name: Indoor and pedestrian navigation
summary: PDR, foot-mounted INS, dismounted soldier navigation, indoor positioning.

name: Autopilots and flight control
summary: Flight stacks, control loops, estimation inside autopilots, firmware.

name: MAVLink, ground control and C2 links
summary: MAVLink protocol, SDKs, ground control stations, telemetry radios.

name: Path and motion planning
summary: Global/local planners, sampling and search based planning, trajectory optimization.

name: Mission planning and routing
summary: Route networks, waypoint missions, coverage, terrain-aware and threat-aware routing.

name: Obstacle avoidance and collision avoidance
summary: Reactive avoidance, sense-and-avoid, DAA.

name: Swarms and multi-agent navigation
summary: Cooperative localization, swarm control, multi-robot SLAM, formation flight.

name: GIS, maps and geospatial data
summary: Map engines, tiles, DEMs, orthophotos, coordinate systems, geodesy.

name: Geodesy and coordinate frames
summary: Datums, projections, ECEF/ENU/NED, MGRS, geoid models.

name: Situational awareness and C2 interop
summary: TAK/CoT, MIL-STD-2525/APP-6 symbology, blue force tracking, common operating picture.

name: Maritime navigation
summary: Surface vessel navigation, AIS, ECDIS/charts, USVs.

name: Underwater navigation
summary: DVL, USBL/LBL acoustics, AUV navigation, underwater SLAM.

name: Ground vehicle autonomy
summary: UGV/off-road autonomy stacks, localization and navigation for ground robots.

name: Space and orbital navigation
summary: Orbit determination, LEO-PNT, spacecraft navigation.

name: Simulation and HIL/SITL
summary: Physics and sensor simulators, software/hardware-in-the-loop, GNSS signal simulators.

name: Datasets and benchmarks
summary: Public datasets, evaluation tools, leaderboards for navigation and localization.

name: ROS / ROS 2 robotics middleware
summary: ROS ecosystem packages for navigation and localization.

name: Onboard / edge AI perception
summary: Detection, segmentation, depth on embedded hardware supporting navigation.

name: Tracking and data association
summary: Multi-target tracking, MHT/JPDA, track fusion (for nav-relevant awareness, not weapon guidance).

name: Counter-UAS and drone detection

name: Electronic warfare resilience

name: Standards and interface specs
summary: ICDs, STANAGs, RTCM, NMEA, MAVLink, CoT, ASTERIX, interoperability specs.

name: Policy, export control and ethics
summary: ITAR/EAR, dual-use rules, PNT policy, responsible military AI.

name: LLM agents for robotics and navigation
summary: Language models driving robots, mission planning, MCP servers for drones/ROS/GIS.

name: WildNav
summary: Python pipeline that localizes a drone by matching its downward camera frames against georeferenced satellite map tiles with SuperGlue, then converts the best match into GPS coordinates. Companion code to the 'Vision-based GNSS-Free Localization for UAVs in the Wild' paper.
why_it_matters: The canonical small, readable reference for absolute visual localization over non-urban terrain - exactly the 'visual GPS' building block a GNSS-denied team needs.
hackathon_notes: Clone, drop in your own map tiles with corner coordinates and a few drone photos; runs on a laptop GPU. Brute-force tile search is slow - add a retrieval stage (AnyLoc/SALAD) to prune candidates.

name: visual_localization (GNSS-free UAV)
summary: A cleaner reimplementation of the WildNav idea: match UAV images to satellite tiles with SuperPoint/SuperGlue-style matchers and estimate geographic position.
why_it_matters: Packaged, modular take on the WildNav approach that is easier to extend with newer matchers.
hackathon_notes: Good starting skeleton if WildNav's scripts feel too ad hoc; swap the matcher for LightGlue or XFeat for speed.

name: UAVLocalization (map retrieval + alignment)
summary: Geo-localization system for aerial platforms that first retrieves the right satellite map region with a deep descriptor and then aligns the drone orthophoto to it to extract coordinates; evaluated on reorganized public AgEagle datasets and a field test.
why_it_matters: Shows the two-stage retrieve-then-align architecture end to end with field data, the design most practical systems converge on.
hackathon_notes: Use its pipeline layout as the backbone of a demo; datasets need a separate download. Conda env file provided.

name: AnyVisLoc benchmark
summary: Benchmark and code for UAV absolute visual localization under low-altitude, multi-view (oblique) observation, comparing retrieval and matching combinations against aerial and satellite reference maps.
why_it_matters: One of the most up-to-date (2025) systematic comparisons of what actually works for low-altitude drones, which is the regime of small tactical UAVs.
hackathon_notes: Read its results before choosing a retrieval/matcher combo; reuse its evaluation scripts to score your own pipeline.

name: U2S-CVGL (scale-aware UAV-to-satellite)
summary: Scale-aware cross-view geo-localization method for matching UAV views to satellite imagery when the altitude-driven scale difference is unknown.
why_it_matters: Scale mismatch is one of the main failure modes when flight altitude is uncertain; this targets it directly.
hackathon_notes: Research code; useful if your demo flies at varying altitudes and fixed-scale tiles break.

name: GNSS-Denied UAV Geolocalization (terrain-weighted)
summary: Code and demos for a UAV geolocalization system that combines image matching, visual odometry and a terrain-weighted constraint optimization, intended to work day and night.
why_it_matters: Fuses absolute map matches with relative VO and terrain constraints - the hybrid structure a real GNSS-denied nav stack needs.
hackathon_notes: Check what is actually released before planning around it; mainly a reference for the fusion design.

name: GeoAnchor
summary: Recent project fusing visual odometry with satellite-map matching in a particle filter for GNSS-denied UAV flight, with an explicit notion of when the map match should not be trusted; evaluated on UAV-VisLoc flights and with a browser demo.
why_it_matters: Directly addresses the practical problem that per-frame map matching often fails (water, farmland, repetitive texture), and shows how to bridge with VO.
hackathon_notes: Very recent single-author project; good blueprint for a 48h demo combining VO drift with intermittent absolute fixes. Verify numbers yourself.

name: KF-HomoVAL
summary: 6-DoF absolute visual localization for UAVs built on deep homography estimation between the drone view and a reference map, smoothed with a Kalman filter.
why_it_matters: Homography-based registration gives full pose, not just a location, which helps when the camera is not nadir.
hackathon_notes: Pair with the STHN family for comparison; expect to retrain on your imagery.

name: UAVision
summary: Map-matching-based visual localization software for UAVs in GNSS-denied settings, shipped with a GUI front end and demo.
why_it_matters: One of the few projects packaged as an operator-facing tool rather than a paper repo.
hackathon_notes: Useful for UI inspiration and a quick demo; inspect the matcher it uses before relying on accuracy.

name: Visual Locator
summary: Absolute drone positioning by image retrieval (SelaVPR-style ViT features) over cropped satellite tiles followed by registration with SIFT+RANSAC or SuperPoint+SuperGlue.
why_it_matters: Clean example of a retrieval + registration pipeline that compares classic and learned matchers side by side.
hackathon_notes: Training described used a multi-GPU server; for a hackathon reuse pretrained weights and the pipeline code only.

name: Aerial Template Matching
summary: Classical template-matching approach for locating an aerial image inside a larger reference image, built on OpenCV.
why_it_matters: A zero-training baseline to compare learned matchers against; mirrors classic DSMAC-style scene correlation in spirit.
hackathon_notes: Runs instantly; good as a fallback or ablation baseline in a demo.

name: CrossLoc
summary: CVPR 2022 cross-modal visual representation learning for absolute camera localization of aerial imagery, trained largely on synthetic data rendered from geodata.
why_it_matters: Shows that synthetic renders from DEM/orthophoto can train localizers for real flights - a cheap way to cover new terrain.
hackathon_notes: Older and heavy to set up; read for the synthetic-data idea.

name: JointLoc
summary: Real-time visual localization framework for planetary UAVs that jointly uses relative and absolute pose estimation against orbital maps.
why_it_matters: Planetary flight is the purest GNSS-free case; the joint relative+absolute design transfers to Earth.
hackathon_notes: C++ build; mostly a design reference.

name: University-1652 baseline
summary: Dataset and baseline code for drone-based geo-localization across drone, satellite and ground views of university buildings worldwide.
why_it_matters: The standard drone-to-satellite retrieval benchmark; most cross-view papers report on it.
hackathon_notes: Dataset requires a request form; the synthetic drone views are building-centric, not wide-area terrain.

name: SUES-200 benchmark
summary: Multi-height, multi-scene drone-satellite cross-view dataset and evaluation code, capturing drone imagery at several altitudes.
why_it_matters: Adds altitude variation that University-1652 lacks - closer to real flight profiles.
hackathon_notes: Use as a second evaluation set alongside University-1652.

name: DenseUAV
summary: Dataset and baseline (TIP 2023) for UAV self-positioning in low-altitude urban environments using dense sampling of drone and satellite views.
why_it_matters: Targets self-positioning (where am I) rather than target retrieval, with dense reference sampling.
hackathon_notes: Good dataset for training a retrieval head for urban flights.

name: Sample4Geo
summary: Cross-view geo-localization training with hard negative sampling, reporting strong results on drone-satellite and street-satellite benchmarks with a simple contrastive setup.
why_it_matters: A strong, simple baseline that is easy to retrain for your own drone/satellite pairs.
hackathon_notes: Pretrained checkpoints help; fine-tune on your tile set if time allows.

name: LPN (Local Pattern Network)
summary: PyTorch implementation of a cross-view geo-localization method that pools features in rings around the image center to capture contextual local patterns.
why_it_matters: Widely used baseline in drone-satellite retrieval; useful to understand rotation-robust pooling.
hackathon_notes: Mainly as a comparison baseline.

name: UAV-VisLoc dataset
summary: Large-scale dataset of real UAV flight imagery with satellite reference maps for UAV visual localization across varied terrain.
why_it_matters: Real nadir-ish drone frames with ground truth over large, non-urban areas - the closest public match to a GNSS-denied flight test.
hackathon_notes: Best dataset to test a visual-GPS demo; pick one flight and its map, run your matcher, plot error vs ground truth.

name: Satellite-thermal geo-localization
summary: IROS 2023 code for long-range UAV thermal geo-localization against satellite RGB imagery, using domain adaptation to bridge thermal and visible imagery; comes with the Boson-nighttime dataset.
why_it_matters: Night flight is when GNSS-denied UAVs are most exposed; this is the main open line of work for thermal-to-satellite matching.
hackathon_notes: Dataset on Hugging Face (gated). Use the pretrained model to show night-time matching in a demo.

name: STHN
summary: Deep homography estimation for aligning UAV thermal images to satellite maps (RA-L 2024), refining coarse geo-localization into precise alignment.
why_it_matters: Turns a coarse thermal match into an accurate position fix.
hackathon_notes: Combine with the IROS 2023 retrieval stage from the same lab.

name: UASTHN
summary: ICRA 2025 extension of STHN that adds uncertainty estimation to satellite-thermal homography, so the system can say when a fix is unreliable.
why_it_matters: Calibrated uncertainty is what lets a nav filter safely ingest visual fixes.
hackathon_notes: Feed its uncertainty into your EKF measurement covariance.

name: SCC-Loc
summary: Zero-shot UAV thermal geo-localization against satellite imagery without thermal-specific training.
why_it_matters: Zero-shot avoids collecting paired thermal data, a common blocker.
hackathon_notes: Very recent; check release completeness.

name: Seasonally invariant transform (visual TRN)
summary: Training code for a learned image transform that makes aerial imagery robust to seasonal appearance change for visual terrain-relative navigation.
why_it_matters: Reference maps are often from a different season than the flight; this attacks that gap.
hackathon_notes: Older; reference for appearance-change preprocessing.

name: CELL
summary: Event camera localization in prior lidar maps with confidence weighting.
why_it_matters: Event cameras keep working in low light and fast motion, relevant for night localization against a prior map.
hackathon_notes: Requires event camera data; mostly a reference.

name: AnyLoc
summary: Universal visual place recognition using foundation-model (DINOv2) features with VLAD/GeM aggregation, working across aerial, underwater, indoor and outdoor domains without task-specific training.
why_it_matters: Training-free retrieval that already works on aerial imagery - the fastest way to get a coarse 'which tile am I over' stage.
hackathon_notes: Extract descriptors for your satellite tiles offline, query with drone frames; then refine with LightGlue/RoMa.

name: hloc
summary: Toolbox for hierarchical visual localization: global retrieval (NetVLAD etc.) to find candidate images, then local feature matching (SuperPoint, LightGlue...) and PnP against an SfM model.
why_it_matters: The standard plumbing for coarse-to-fine localization; ready-made wrappers for most retrieval and matching models.
hackathon_notes: Use its retrieval + matching APIs even without the SfM part; pip-installable.

name: EigenPlaces
summary: ICCV 2023 visual place recognition training method for viewpoint-robust descriptors.
why_it_matters: Viewpoint robustness matters when drone heading and tilt vary against nadir satellite tiles.
hackathon_notes: Pretrained models loadable via torch.hub.

name: CosPlace
summary: CVPR 2022 large-scale visual geo-localization treating place recognition as classification over geographic cells.
why_it_matters: Scales to very large maps, a useful framing for country-sized reference databases.
hackathon_notes: torch.hub weights available.

name: SALAD
summary: Place recognition descriptor using optimal-transport aggregation of DINOv2 features.
why_it_matters: Among the strongest off-the-shelf retrieval descriptors; good drop-in for the coarse stage.
hackathon_notes: Load via torch.hub, compare with AnyLoc on your tiles.

name: MixVPR
summary: WACV 2023 place recognition descriptor built by MLP feature mixing; lightweight and fast.
why_it_matters: Compact descriptors suit embedded retrieval on a drone.
hackathon_notes: Fast inference; good for an onboard-feasibility story.

name: BoQ
summary: CVPR 2024 place recognition with a bag of learnable global queries over backbone features.
why_it_matters: Recent strong retrieval model with simple usage.
hackathon_notes: torch.hub available.

name: SelaVPR
summary: ICLR 2024 method adapting pretrained foundation models for place recognition with lightweight adapters, producing both global and local features.
why_it_matters: Global+local output lets one model do retrieval and re-ranking.
hackathon_notes: Used by Visual-Locator for UAV retrieval.

name: VPR methods evaluation
summary: Wrapper exposing many state-of-the-art place recognition models behind one interface so you can switch models with one parameter.
why_it_matters: Fastest way to benchmark several retrieval models on your own drone/satellite set.
hackathon_notes: Format your data as database/queries folders with UTM in filenames; GPU recommended.

name: LightGlue
summary: Fast learned local feature matcher (ICCV 2023) that adapts its depth to pair difficulty; works with SuperPoint, DISK, ALIKED and SIFT features.
why_it_matters: The default fine-matching stage for drone-to-tile registration today: accurate and fast enough for near-real-time.
hackathon_notes: pip install; use SuperPoint+LightGlue between a drone frame and top-k retrieved tiles, then RANSAC homography.

name: Glue Factory
summary: Training library for local feature detection and matching (trains LightGlue and others).
why_it_matters: Lets you fine-tune a matcher on aerial/satellite pairs if off-the-shelf models struggle.
hackathon_notes: Training takes longer than a hackathon; use for post-event work.

name: SuperGlue (pretrained)
summary: Pretrained SuperGlue graph-neural-network matcher with SuperPoint features (CVPR 2020).
why_it_matters: Used by WildNav and many UAV localization repos; non-commercial license limits reuse.
hackathon_notes: Prefer LightGlue (permissive license, faster) unless replicating WildNav exactly.

name: SuperPoint (pretrained)
summary: Pretrained SuperPoint keypoint detector and descriptor.
why_it_matters: Feature front end for SuperGlue/LightGlue pipelines.
hackathon_notes: Most users get SuperPoint via LightGlue/hloc now.

name: LoFTR
summary: Detector-free transformer matcher producing dense-ish correspondences, good on low-texture scenes.
why_it_matters: Low-texture terrain (fields, desert) breaks keypoint matchers; detector-free matching helps.
hackathon_notes: Also available in kornia for easy use.

name: RoMa
summary: Robust dense feature matcher (CVPR 2024) estimating pixel-dense warps with certainties, strong under large appearance change.
why_it_matters: Handles season, lighting and sensor differences between drone frames and satellite imagery better than sparse matchers, at higher compute cost.
hackathon_notes: Use as the accurate-but-slow verifier on the top retrieval hit; GPU recommended.

name: MASt3R
summary: Matching grounded in 3D: predicts dense correspondences and 3D pointmaps from image pairs, building on DUSt3R.
why_it_matters: Robust to extreme viewpoint change (oblique drone view vs nadir satellite) because it reasons in 3D.
hackathon_notes: Heavy model and non-commercial license; good for offline demos.

name: XFeat
summary: Lightweight local feature extractor and matcher (CVPR 2024) designed for speed on constrained hardware.
why_it_matters: Fits onboard compute on small drones where LightGlue on GPU is not available.
hackathon_notes: Runs on CPU in real time; good for an embedded/Jetson story.

name: vismatch (image-matching-models)
summary: Wrapper exposing 50+ image matching models behind one interface (formerly image-matching-models).
why_it_matters: Swap SIFT, LightGlue, LoFTR, RoMa, MASt3R etc. with one line to find the best matcher for your imagery.
hackathon_notes: Best first stop for matcher selection during the hackathon.

name: python-tercom
summary: Python demo of TERCOM terrain contour matching: simulate a radar-altimeter profile over a DEM and correlate it against the map to recover position.
why_it_matters: Smallest end-to-end TERCOM sim to understand and extend for a DEM-matching demo.
hackathon_notes: Load an SRTM/Copernicus DEM tile, generate a profile, show the correlation surface; an afternoon's work.

name: tercom_nav (TERCOM + ESKF)
summary: ROS 2 package combining TERCOM-style terrain matching with an error-state Kalman filter for UAV navigation.
why_it_matters: Bridges batch terrain matching into a recursive filter that a real autopilot stack could consume.
hackathon_notes: Good if your team runs ROS 2 with PX4/ArduPilot SITL; pair with a DEM and simulated altimeter.

name: TERCOM via particle filter
summary: MATLAB SIR particle filter estimating UAV position from terrain contour matching in GPS-denied flight.
why_it_matters: Particle filters handle the multimodal ambiguity of terrain matching better than a single correlation peak.
hackathon_notes: Port the filter loop to Python for a demo.

name: TERCOM-python (TERCOM + DSMAC)
summary: OpenCV-based demo of map-based navigation combining terrain contour matching with scene-matching area correlation.
why_it_matters: Shows both classic map-matching families side by side.
hackathon_notes: Small educational code; use for concept slides and quick baselines.

name: terrain-nav-preprocessing
summary: Preprocessing tools for terrain-referenced navigation, generating DEM tiles with controlled noise for training and evaluation.
why_it_matters: Saves time preparing DEM data for TRN experiments.
hackathon_notes: Use to build synthetic DEM test sets.

name: MagNav.jl
summary: Julia package from the DAF-MIT AI Accelerator for airborne magnetic anomaly navigation: flight/INS data import or simulation, anomaly maps, aircraft magnetic compensation (Tolles-Lawson and neural models) and navigation filters.
why_it_matters: Official code behind the AFRL/MIT MagNav challenge; magnetic navigation is a leading GNSS-independent, unjammable PNT approach in DIU and AFRL programs.
hackathon_notes: Julia install plus large data download; first run compiles slowly. Start from the example notebooks and the provided flight lines.

name: MagNavPy
summary: Python port of MagNav.jl for magnetic navigation research.
why_it_matters: Lowers the language barrier to the MagNav data and algorithms for Python-heavy teams.
hackathon_notes: Young community port; verify results against MagNav.jl outputs before trusting.

name: MAMMAL
summary: Python package (Magnetic Anomaly Map Matching Airborne and Land) for simulating and processing aeromagnetic survey data and building anomaly maps for MagNav.
why_it_matters: Map creation is the hidden half of MagNav; this covers it in Python.
hackathon_notes: Use to generate maps or simulated surveys feeding a particle filter.

name: AFIT MagNav example data
summary: Sample data for MagNav work: MIT-AIA anomaly maps, a challenge flight, North American magnetic anomaly grids and geoid files.
why_it_matters: Ready-made data so a team can start without hunting for maps.
hackathon_notes: Grab these files first.

name: Rao-Blackwellized SLAM smoothing (magnetic)
summary: MATLAB code for Rao-Blackwellized particle smoothing for SLAM, including magnetic field mapping and map-matching localization with a magnetometer.
why_it_matters: Clean academic reference for magnetic field SLAM and particle-filter matching at small scale.
hackathon_notes: Good for understanding magnetic map matching quickly.

name: MagNav deep-learning compensation
summary: Deep-learning approach to aircraft magnetic disturbance compensation built around the MagNav challenge data.
why_it_matters: Compensation quality dominates MagNav accuracy; shows a learned alternative to Tolles-Lawson.
hackathon_notes: Unmaintained since 2023; dependencies may need pinning.

name: DroneMagNav
summary: Open hardware + firmware design for a drone magnetic-anomaly navigation board (ESP32-S3, magnetometer, IMU, baro) running particle-filter matching against a global anomaly map and feeding position to a flight controller over MAVLink.
why_it_matters: Rare example of MagNav pushed down to cheap drone hardware with an autopilot interface.
hackathon_notes: Very recent single-author project; hardware not validated in flight per what we could see. Global anomaly maps are coarse, so expect km-level, not meter-level, results on small drones.

name: tetra3
summary: Fast lost-in-space plate solver for star trackers from ESA: identifies stars in an image and returns attitude using a precomputed pattern database.
why_it_matters: Star-based attitude (and with time + gravity vector, position) is jam-proof; tetra3 is the easiest open solver.
hackathon_notes: Not on PyPI: pip install git+https://github.com/esa/tetra3.git; solve sample images in minutes. Combine attitude with a level sensor and clock for a celestial fix demo.

name: cedar-solve
summary: Actively maintained fork of tetra3 with speed and robustness improvements, used in the Cedar telescope-aiming product.
why_it_matters: More maintained than upstream tetra3 for new work.
hackathon_notes: Drop-in alternative to tetra3.

name: OpenStarTracker
summary: Open-source star tracker using a Bayesian star identification approach, developed by the University at Buffalo Nanosatellite Lab.
why_it_matters: Full camera-to-attitude pipeline with calibration, proven on small-satellite hardware.
hackathon_notes: Calibration step needed for your camera; budget a few hours.

name: LOST
summary: Open-source star tracker (C++) covering centroiding, star identification and attitude estimation, from the UW CubeSat team.
why_it_matters: Compiled, modular alternative for embedded targets.
hackathon_notes: Build with make; includes test images.

name: NASA COTS Star Tracker
summary: NASA software for building a star tracker from commercial off-the-shelf cameras, including calibration and attitude solution.
why_it_matters: Directly aimed at cheap COTS cameras - the hardware a hackathon team will have.
hackathon_notes: Follow its calibration workflow with a phone or Pi camera.

name: Deep learning celestial navigation
summary: Exploratory project on automating celestial navigation with deep learning and edge inference on synthetic sky images.
why_it_matters: Shows a learning-based route from sky images to position.
hackathon_notes: Concept reference.

name: celestial-navigation toolkit
summary: Python toolkit for classic celestial navigation sight reduction, usable offline on a phone.
why_it_matters: Ground-truth math for turning star/sun sightings into a position.
hackathon_notes: Pair with a star tracker output to compute position.

name: ccompass
summary: Header-only C library for processing sky polarization images to support heading estimation; successor to compyss.
why_it_matters: Polarization compass gives heading without magnetometers or GNSS, robust to magnetic disturbance.
hackathon_notes: Needs a polarization camera (or simulated images).

name: Starlink LEO-PNT
summary: Passive positioning using Starlink downlink signals as signals of opportunity: SDR capture, blind OFDM analysis, Doppler extraction, TDOA/FDOA solver and EKF with TLE-based orbits.
why_it_matters: One of the very few open end-to-end attempts at Starlink-based PNT, a hot GNSS-alternative topic.
hackathon_notes: Needs an SDR that covers Ku-band via LNB, or use the simulation path with TLEs. Treat claims as unverified.

name: LEO SoOP positioning thesis (Voska)
summary: Diploma thesis materials on signals-of-opportunity positioning from LEO satellites using Doppler shift and TLE-based orbits.
why_it_matters: Readable derivation plus code for Doppler positioning from LEO constellations.
hackathon_notes: Use as the math reference for a Doppler-positioning simulator.

name: LEO-SPINE
summary: Open toolkit for LEO/MEO/GEO constellation simulation and single/multi-satellite positioning.
why_it_matters: Lets a team simulate LEO-based positioning geometry and accuracy without hardware.
hackathon_notes: Browser-friendly; good for visualizing LEO coverage in a pitch.

name: GraphGNSSLib LEO
summary: Factor-graph positioning combining GNSS and LEO satellite measurements, extending GraphGNSSLib.
why_it_matters: Shows how LEO observations slot into a factor graph alongside degraded GNSS.
hackathon_notes: C/ROS build; reference.

name: A Tutorial on 5G Positioning (code)
summary: MATLAB simulation code accompanying an IEEE tutorial on 5G positioning (timing, angle and multi-cell methods).
why_it_matters: Cellular positioning is a fallback PNT source; this is a didactic, runnable starting point.
hackathon_notes: MATLAB needed (Octave may partly work).

name: KiwiSDR
summary: Web-accessible shortwave SDR receiver (10 kHz - 30 MHz) with built-in software GPS and a Loran-C/eLoran monitor extension.
why_it_matters: Public KiwiSDR network offers remote access to LF signals for eLoran/Loran experiments without owning hardware.
hackathon_notes: Use public KiwiSDR receivers to look at LF navigation signals; not a positioning solver.

name: PX4 Autopilot
summary: Dronecode flight stack for multirotors, fixed-wing, VTOL, rovers and boats, built on NuttX with a uORB pub/sub middleware. Its EKF2 estimator fuses IMU, GNSS, baro, magnetometer, optical flow, range finders and external vision.
why_it_matters: The most common permissive-licensed (BSD) autopilot base for defense and commercial UAS; EKF2 external-vision and flow fusion is the standard route to GPS-denied flight.
hackathon_notes: Run `make px4_sitl gz_x500` for SITL with Gazebo in under an hour. Feed VIO/SLAM poses via the ROS 2 uXRCE-DDS bridge or MAVLink ODOMETRY; disable GPS with EKF2_GPS_CTRL to test GPS-denied behaviour.

name: ArduPilot
summary: GPL autopilot covering Copter, Plane (incl. QuadPlane VTOL), Rover, boats and ArduSub, plus AP_Periph CAN peripherals. EKF3 supports switchable source sets, so GNSS, optical flow, beacons, wheel odometry and external vision can be swapped in flight.
why_it_matters: Very broad vehicle coverage and mature non-GPS navigation docs; EKF3 source switching (EK3_SRCn_*) is directly useful for GNSS-loss and spoofing-resilience experiments.
hackathon_notes: `sim_vehicle.py -v ArduCopter --console --map` gives SITL in minutes. Lua scripting lets you add behaviour on the flight controller without a fork. Use SIM_GPS1_ENABLE=0 / EK3_SRC1_* to simulate GNSS denial.

name: INAV
summary: Navigation-focused fork of the Cleanflight/Betaflight lineage for small multirotors, fixed-wing and rovers, adding GPS position hold, return-to-home and waypoint missions on cheap F4/F7/H7 boards.
why_it_matters: Lowest-cost path to GNSS waypoint navigation on FPV-class airframes; useful to show how small drones behave on GNSS loss and how RTH failsafes work.
hackathon_notes: Configure with INAV Configurator; supports MSP and a MAVLink telemetry subset. SITL exists but is less polished than PX4/ArduPilot. Good for physical demos on cheap hardware.

name: Betaflight
summary: Racing/freestyle-oriented flight controller firmware focused on attitude control and low-latency filtering; GPS rescue mode is its main navigation feature.
why_it_matters: Dominant firmware on FPV drones seen in current conflicts; understanding its limited navigation (GPS Rescue only) matters for C-UAS and EW-impact analysis.
hackathon_notes: Not a navigation platform; use for FPV-class hardware or to study how small drones react to link loss and GNSS jamming.

name: Paparazzi UAV
summary: Long-running academic autopilot (ENAC, TU Delft and others) for fixed-wing, rotorcraft and hybrids, with its own ground segment, flight-plan language and INS modules.
why_it_matters: Strong research heritage in fixed-wing and micro air vehicles, including vision-based and swarm experiments; a non-MAVLink reference architecture.
hackathon_notes: Toolchain and ground station setup takes hours; pick only if you know it already. Flight-plan XML is a nice example of declarative mission logic.

name: LibrePilot
summary: GitHub mirror of LibrePilot, the community continuation of OpenPilot for CC3D/Revolution boards, with the GCS bundled. Main development was on Bitbucket and has been quiet for years.
why_it_matters: Historical reference for the OpenPilot-era INS13 estimator and UAVTalk protocol; not a base for new work.
hackathon_notes: Read-only reference. Hardware is end-of-life.

name: OpenPilot (mirror)
summary: Mirror of the original OpenPilot flight controller project (not comma.ai's openpilot), frozen since 2015.
why_it_matters: Origin of the TauLabs, dRonin and LibrePilot family; historical only.
hackathon_notes: Historical reference only.

name: dRehmFlight VTOL
summary: Single-file Arduino/Teensy flight controller for small VTOL and multirotor craft, written to be read and modified by students.
why_it_matters: Easiest flight-control code to understand end to end; good for teaching attitude estimation (Madgwick) and control loops in a weekend.
hackathon_notes: Flash to a Teensy with an MPU6050/9250 IMU; no navigation or MAVLink, so pair with a companion for anything beyond stabilisation.

name: ESP-Drone
summary: Espressif's mini quadcopter firmware for ESP32/ESP32-S2/S3, derived from Crazyflie code, controlled over Wi-Fi.
why_it_matters: Very cheap, hackable airframe with Wi-Fi control; usable for indoor swarm or RF experiments.
hackathon_notes: Builds with ESP-IDF; supports optical-flow deck style positioning only with extra sensors. Expect tuning effort on DIY frames.

name: Crazyflie firmware
summary: Firmware for the Crazyflie nano quad, Bolt and the Roadrunner positioning tag, with EKF and complementary estimators supporting UWB Loco positioning, Lighthouse, Flow deck and mocap.
why_it_matters: Mature indoor research platform where UWB/Lighthouse localisation and GPS-free estimation are first-class; widely used in swarm papers.
hackathon_notes: If you have Crazyflies, the Python lib gets you scripted flights in an hour. UWB Loco anchors make a good GNSS-denied testbed. Simulation via crazyswarm2 or the official SIL.

name: cflib (Crazyflie Python library)
summary: Python API to connect, log, set parameters and send setpoints/high-level commands to Crazyflies over Crazyradio or USB.
why_it_matters: Fastest way to script autonomy experiments on nano drones.
hackathon_notes: pip install cflib; Swarm class runs parallel commands.

name: Crazyswarm2
summary: ROS 2 framework for flying many Crazyflie nano-quadrotors with motion capture or onboard localization, including simulation backends.
why_it_matters: Ready-made multi-agent testbed for coordinated indoor flight and formation experiments.
hackathon_notes: Simulation works without hardware; with Crazyflies plus Loco or Lighthouse you can fly a small swarm in a day.

name: ROSflight firmware
summary: Lean research autopilot (BYU) that keeps only attitude estimation and low-level control on the flight board and pushes everything else to a ROS companion.
why_it_matters: Clean split between embedded and onboard autonomy; good for teams who want full control of the estimator on the companion.
hackathon_notes: Use with rosflight_ros_pkgs; includes a simulator so hardware is optional.

name: ROSflight ROS packages
summary: ROS 2 interface, simulator and utilities for the ROSflight autopilot.
why_it_matters: Companion-side half of ROSflight, where navigation and autonomy live.
hackathon_notes: Start with the sim launch files.

name: PX4 ECL (Estimation & Control Library)
summary: Former home of PX4's estimation and control library including the EKF2 navigation filter; archived after the code moved into PX4-Autopilot.
why_it_matters: Its history and docs remain a readable reference for the EKF2 derivation (SymPy-generated equations).
hackathon_notes: Read the current EKF2 in PX4-Autopilot src/modules/ekf2 instead; use this for history.

name: PX4 OpticalFlow
summary: Algorithms for computing optical flow from a downward camera to produce velocity inputs for a position estimator.
why_it_matters: Optical flow plus range finder is the cheapest GNSS-free velocity source for low-altitude hover and drift control.
hackathon_notes: Can run on a companion and publish OPTICAL_FLOW_RAD over MAVLink; check activity before depending on it.

name: MAVLink
summary: Message definitions (XML dialects) and the pymavlink-based generator for the MAVLink micro air vehicle protocol, used by PX4, ArduPilot and most GCS tools.
why_it_matters: The lingua franca of open-source UAS; any GCS, companion, Remote ID or C-UAS sensor integration ends up speaking it.
hackathon_notes: Add a custom dialect XML and regenerate bindings to prototype new messages (e.g. a jamming-detection report).

name: MAVLink Developer Guide
summary: Source of the mavlink.io documentation: protocol, microservices (mission, parameters, camera, Open Drone ID) and message reference.
why_it_matters: Canonical reference when wiring new sensors or services over MAVLink.
hackathon_notes: Read the microservice pages before implementing anything stateful.

name: pymavlink
summary: Python MAVLink implementation plus tools for connections, log parsing (DataFlash/tlog) and code generation.
why_it_matters: Quickest path to scripting a vehicle or parsing flight logs to evaluate estimator behaviour under GNSS loss.
hackathon_notes: pip install pymavlink; mavutil.mavlink_connection('udp:...') against SITL works in minutes.

name: MAVSDK
summary: C++ SDK exposing high-level MAVLink plugins (action, mission, offboard, telemetry, camera) with a gRPC server for other languages.
why_it_matters: Clean API for companion-side autonomy against PX4 (and to a degree ArduPilot) without ROS.
hackathon_notes: Use MAVSDK-Python for hackathon speed; mavsdk_server is bundled.

name: MAVSDK-Python
summary: Asyncio Python client for MAVSDK that wraps a bundled mavsdk_server.
why_it_matters: Probably the fastest way to script missions or offboard control against PX4 SITL.
hackathon_notes: pip install mavsdk-grpc and import mavsdk_grpc (the PyPI name 'mavsdk' now means the native binding with a different API); examples cover takeoff, missions, offboard velocity.

name: MAVROS
summary: ROS/ROS 2 node bridging MAVLink to ROS topics and services, with GCS proxy; widely used to push vision/SLAM poses into PX4 or ArduPilot.
why_it_matters: Standard glue between ROS-based VIO/SLAM and a flight controller for GPS-denied navigation.
hackathon_notes: Publish to /mavros/vision_pose/pose or odometry topics; mind ENU/NED frame conversions.

name: mavlink-router
summary: Lightweight C++ daemon that routes MAVLink between serial, UDP and TCP endpoints with filtering and logging.
why_it_matters: Typical companion-computer plumbing to share one flight-controller link between GCS, autonomy and loggers.
hackathon_notes: Build with meson; one config file. Run it before attaching multiple clients.

name: mavp2p
summary: Single-binary Go MAVLink router/proxy supporting serial, UDP and TCP with deduplication.
why_it_matters: Zero-dependency alternative to mavlink-router; easy to drop on any companion.
hackathon_notes: Download the release binary and run; no build.

name: gomavlib
summary: Go MAVLink v1/v2 library with dialect generation and multiple transports.
why_it_matters: Good for writing small, robust Go services (telemetry relays, sensor bridges).
hackathon_notes: Go modules; examples for reading/writing messages.

name: rust-mavlink
summary: Rust implementation of MAVLink with generated dialects and serial/UDP/TCP connections.
why_it_matters: Memory-safe option for ground or embedded services.
hackathon_notes: cargo add mavlink.

name: node-mavlink
summary: TypeScript/Node.js MAVLink bindings and tools.
why_it_matters: Handy for web dashboards and Node-based ground tools.
hackathon_notes: npm install; works over serial/UDP/TCP.

name: DroneKit-Python
summary: Older high-level Python API for MAVLink vehicles, built on pymavlink; maintenance has slowed (last push 2024).
why_it_matters: Many tutorials still use it; fine for simple ArduPilot scripts but prefer pymavlink or MAVSDK for new work.
hackathon_notes: Has compatibility issues with recent Python versions; pin Python 3.9/3.10 or avoid.

name: MAVProxy
summary: Command-line, module-based ground station and MAVLink proxy with map, console and many plugins.
why_it_matters: Default SITL console for ArduPilot; scriptable modules make it easy to prototype operator-side tools.
hackathon_notes: Comes with sim_vehicle.py; write a module to add custom displays or alerts (e.g. GNSS anomaly warnings).

name: QGroundControl
summary: Qt/QML cross-platform GCS (desktop, Android, iOS) for PX4 and ArduPilot: setup, mission planning, video and telemetry.
why_it_matters: Most common open GCS; a base for custom operator UIs, including Remote ID display.
hackathon_notes: Use prebuilt binaries for SITL; custom builds take a few hours to set up Qt.

name: Mission Planner
summary: Windows-centric C#/.NET GCS for ArduPilot with deep parameter, log-analysis and mission tooling.
why_it_matters: Feature-richest ArduPilot GCS; the EKF and GPS status views are useful during GNSS-denial tests.
hackathon_notes: Windows best; runs under Mono on Linux/mac with caveats.

name: APM Planner 2
summary: Qt-based cross-platform ArduPilot GCS, now largely in maintenance mode.
why_it_matters: Alternative GCS mainly of historical interest.
hackathon_notes: Prefer QGroundControl or Mission Planner.

name: PX4 Flight Review
summary: Web app for uploading and plotting PX4 ULog flight logs, including estimator innovations and test ratios.
why_it_matters: Fast way to judge whether EKF2 is healthy when fusing a new vision or flow source.
hackathon_notes: Use the hosted instance or run locally with Docker.

name: UAV Log Viewer
summary: Browser-based viewer for ArduPilot DataFlash and MAVLink logs (also reads PX4 ULog), with 3D replay and plotting.
why_it_matters: Quick post-flight review of EKF3 innovations and source switching.
hackathon_notes: Hosted at plot.ardupilot.org; no install.

name: ArduPilot Methodic Configurator
summary: Guided step-by-step parameter configuration tool for ArduPilot vehicles.
why_it_matters: Reduces setup mistakes on new airframes, which matter more than code in short builds.
hackathon_notes: Use when building physical ArduPilot vehicles.

name: px4_msgs
summary: ROS 2 message definitions mirroring PX4 uORB topics, used with the uXRCE-DDS bridge.
why_it_matters: Required to talk to PX4 natively from ROS 2 (e.g. VehicleOdometry for external vision).
hackathon_notes: Match the branch to your PX4 version or messages will mismatch.

name: px4_ros_com
summary: Example ROS 2 nodes and helpers (frame transforms) for interfacing with PX4 over DDS.
why_it_matters: Starting templates for offboard control and sending odometry into PX4.
hackathon_notes: Clone alongside px4_msgs into a colcon workspace.

name: Micro XRCE-DDS Agent
summary: Agent that bridges DDS-XRCE clients on microcontrollers into a full DDS / ROS 2 graph; PX4 and ArduPilot use it for native ROS 2.
why_it_matters: Core link in the PX4 and ArduPilot ROS 2 (DDS) paths.
hackathon_notes: Install via snap or build from source; run MicroXRCEAgent udp4 -p 8888 for SITL.

name: PX4 ROS 2 Interface Library
summary: C++ library for writing PX4 flight modes and navigation-data sources in ROS 2 on a companion computer, registered with PX4 as first-class modes.
why_it_matters: Lets a team ship a custom autonomy mode or inject a local/global position estimate (e.g. a visual geolocalisation fix) cleanly into PX4.
hackathon_notes: Needs recent PX4 (1.15+) and matching px4_msgs; examples include custom modes and external navigation interfaces.

name: ROS2 PX4 Offboard Example
summary: Small example of driving PX4 velocity setpoints from ROS 2 teleop, with SITL launch files.
why_it_matters: Good minimal starter for a ROS 2 offboard demo.
hackathon_notes: Runs against PX4 SITL in about an hour.

name: ardupilot_ros
summary: ROS 2 integration examples for ArduPilot, including Cartographer-based non-GPS navigation and Nav2 setups.
why_it_matters: Directly targets lidar-SLAM-fed GPS-free flight on ArduPilot.
hackathon_notes: Use with ardupilot_gz for simulation; follow the wiki ROS 2 pages.

name: ardupilot_gz
summary: ROS 2 + Gazebo packages for ArduPilot SITL integration and testing.
why_it_matters: Gives a ready simulated vehicle with lidar/cameras for ROS 2 navigation experiments.
hackathon_notes: Target ROS 2 Humble + Gazebo Harmonic per the README.

name: ardupilot_gazebo
summary: Gazebo Sim plugins and models that connect ArduPilot SITL to Gazebo physics for copters, rovers and boats.
why_it_matters: Brings ArduPilot vehicles (copter, plane, rover, boat) into gz-sim with realistic sensors for nav and autonomy testing.
hackathon_notes: Build against your Gazebo release, run sim_vehicle.py with '-f gazebo-iris --model JSON'. Follow the README's environment variables for model paths.

name: PX4 SITL Gazebo Classic
summary: Plugins, vehicle models and worlds that connect PX4 SITL/HITL to Gazebo Classic, including GPS, IMU, magnetometer, barometer and optical-flow plugins.
why_it_matters: Large existing corpus of tutorials and research setups still target it; the GPS plugin is a common starting point for spoofing and jamming experiments in sim.
hackathon_notes: Works with Ubuntu 20.04/22.04 and Gazebo 11. Gazebo Classic has reached end of life, so prefer gz-sim for new builds unless you need a specific legacy model.

name: PX4 Avoidance
summary: Archived ROS nodes for local planning, global planning and safe landing using depth sensors with PX4.
why_it_matters: Still a useful reference for obstacle avoidance architectures, but unmaintained.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1 only; read for design ideas.

name: Rpanion-server
summary: Web-based companion-computer manager for MAVLink vehicles: telemetry routing, video streaming, logging and network config on Raspberry Pi/Jetson.
why_it_matters: Turnkey companion setup so the team spends time on navigation code rather than plumbing.
hackathon_notes: Flash the prebuilt image to a Pi; manage routing in the browser.

name: BlueOS
summary: Blue Robotics' onboard software platform for ROVs and USVs: web UI, ArduPilot management, MAVLink routing and a Docker extension system on a Raspberry Pi companion computer.
why_it_matters: Strong base for maritime/underwater vehicle builds; extension system makes adding a nav service easy.
hackathon_notes: Most useful with a BlueROV2; extensions are Docker images, so a nav add-on can be packaged quickly.

name: MAVLink Camera Manager
summary: Rust service that exposes cameras as MAVLink camera components and streams video (RTSP/UDP) to GCS.
why_it_matters: Makes onboard cameras discoverable to QGC and BlueOS without custom code.
hackathon_notes: Runs standalone or inside BlueOS.

name: vision_to_mavros
summary: ROS and Python scripts that convert external localisation (fiducials, T265 VIO, SLAM, depth) into MAVROS/MAVLink pose messages, tested on ArduPilot.
why_it_matters: Proven recipe for feeding vision-based localisation into ArduPilot EKF3 for GPS-denied flight; came out of GSoC work.
hackathon_notes: Old (2022) but simple; adapt the non-ROS T265 script to any VIO source.

name: vision_landing
summary: Precision landing using visual fiducial targets, sending LANDING_TARGET messages to ArduPilot.
why_it_matters: Example of vision-based terminal approach for recovery/landing without GNSS accuracy.
hackathon_notes: Needs OpenCV and a camera on the companion; inactive since 2023.

name: OpenHD
summary: Open-source long-range digital HD video and telemetry link over Wi-Fi adapters in monitor mode (wifibroadcast-style), for air and ground units.
why_it_matters: Low-cost resilient video/telemetry downlink for situational awareness; also a reference for link behaviour under interference.
hackathon_notes: Needs supported Wi-Fi cards (RTL8812AU) and SBCs; budget a few hours for imaging.

name: WFB-ng
summary: Long-range packet radio link over raw Wi-Fi injection with FEC, carrying video, MAVLink and IP tunnels.
why_it_matters: Unidirectional broadcast-style link with FEC is more robust to interference than plain Wi-Fi; useful for EW-resilient telemetry experiments.
hackathon_notes: Install on Linux with compatible RTL8812AU/EU cards; key pairs per link.

name: ExpressLRS
summary: Open-source LoRa/FLRC radio control link (2.4 GHz and sub-GHz) with high packet rates, telemetry and MAVLink passthrough modes.
why_it_matters: Dominant open RC link in FPV; its behaviour under jamming and its telemetry options matter for EW-resilience and C-UAS work.
hackathon_notes: Flash with ExpressLRS Configurator; receivers are cheap.

name: mLRS
summary: LoRa-based bidirectional link carrying RC and full MAVLink serial data on 2.4 GHz, 868/915 MHz and 433 MHz.
why_it_matters: Combines control and telemetry over long-range LoRa for ArduPilot/PX4, which is useful where Wi-Fi links fail.
hackathon_notes: Supports several off-the-shelf modules; read the hardware list first.

name: SiK radio firmware
summary: Firmware and tools for Si1000-based telemetry radios (3DR/RFD900 class) carrying MAVLink.
why_it_matters: Classic serial telemetry radio stack; frequency-hopping config is relevant to link robustness.
hackathon_notes: Mostly use stock firmware; configure via AT commands or Mission Planner.

name: ArduRemoteID
summary: ESP32-based Remote ID transmitter firmware implementing ASTM F3411 broadcast (Bluetooth and Wi-Fi) fed from MAVLink or DroneCAN.
why_it_matters: Cheap compliant Remote ID broadcasting, and the transmitter side of any Remote ID-based C-UAS awareness demo.
hackathon_notes: Flash an ESP32-S3/C3 dev board; pair with opendroneid receiver-android to show detection end to end.

name: Open Drone ID Core C
summary: Reference C library for encoding and decoding ASTM F3411 / ASD-STAN Remote ID messages (location, operator, system, auth) for Bluetooth and Wi-Fi broadcast.
why_it_matters: Remote ID is the cooperative layer of airspace awareness and counter-UAS; this library is the canonical message implementation.
hackathon_notes: Builds with CMake in minutes; pair with an ESP32 or phone receiver to decode drone broadcasts and push them to a map or TAK.

name: OpenDroneID Android receiver
summary: Example Android app that listens for Remote ID broadcasts over Bluetooth 4/5 and Wi-Fi Beacon/NaN and shows drones and operators on a map.
why_it_matters: Fastest way to get a working cooperative drone-detection sensor in a hackathon using only phones.
hackathon_notes: Sideload on a recent Android phone; Wi-Fi NaN support depends on handset. Extend to forward detections as CoT to a TAK server.

name: OpenDroneID Linux transmitter
summary: Example Linux transmitter for Remote ID over Bluetooth and Wi-Fi.
why_it_matters: Lets a companion computer broadcast Remote ID for testing receivers.
hackathon_notes: Needs compatible Bluetooth/Wi-Fi chipsets; dormant since 2023.

name: uav_electronic_ids
summary: Arduino classes for several UAV electronic ID formats (ASTM/EU Remote ID, French ID) and UTM interfaces, with ESP32 examples.
why_it_matters: Small, readable alternative Remote ID implementation, including receiver-side sketches.
hackathon_notes: Arduino IDE; inactive since early 2024.

name: DroneCAN libcanard
summary: Minimal C implementation of the DroneCAN protocol used for GNSS, compass, airspeed and other peripherals on CAN.
why_it_matters: Needed to build custom CAN sensors (e.g. an alternative nav sensor) that ArduPilot/PX4 can consume.
hackathon_notes: Use with dronecan/DSDL; mostly for hardware teams.

name: Aerostack2
summary: ROS 2 framework for autonomous multi-aerial-robot systems: platform abstraction (PX4, DJI, Crazyflie, Gazebo), behaviors, mission scripting in Python and BT, and multi-drone coordination.
why_it_matters: One of the few ROS 2 native UAV mission frameworks that spans simulation to several real autopilots, good for multi-drone mission demos.
hackathon_notes: Binary packages for Humble; Python mission API lets you script takeoff/goto/land for several drones quickly.

name: Stone Soup
summary: Open-source Python framework from UK Dstl and partners for developing, running and evaluating tracking and state estimation algorithms: Kalman variants, particle filters, JPDA, MHT, GM-PHD, track management and metrics.
why_it_matters: A government-backed, permissively developed tracking toolkit - the closest thing to a reference library for situational-awareness fusion that defense judges will recognize.
hackathon_notes: pip install stonesoup; tutorials run in Jupyter. Good for fusing ADS-B, Remote ID or DF bearings into tracks on a common picture within a day. Keep it to air-picture awareness, not fire control.

name: ATAK-CIV (DoD release, archived)
summary: The DoD's public source release of the civilian Android Team Awareness Kit: map engine, Cursor-on-Target messaging and plugin SDK.
why_it_matters: TAK is the de facto common operating picture across US/NATO units, so a plugin or CoT feed is an instantly legible demo for defense judges.
hackathon_notes: Archived; use the TAK Product Center repo for current code. Building ATAK from source is heavy - develop a plugin against a prebuilt SDK instead.

name: ATAK-CIV (TAK Product Center)
summary: Source of the civilian Android Team Awareness Kit maintained by the TAK Product Center: map client, plugin SDK and CoT handling.
why_it_matters: The most widely used open tactical map client; plugins let you inject nav and sensor data into a fielded UI.
hackathon_notes: Plugin builds need the matching SDK version; budget half a day for toolchain. Many teams instead feed CoT from Python and just use stock ATAK/iTAK.

name: FreeTAKServer
summary: Open-source Python server compatible with TAK clients (ATAK, WinTAK, iTAK) that relays Cursor-on-Target positions, chat and data packages.
why_it_matters: Gives dismounted users and robots a shared map picture; common endpoint for drone-detection and blue-force feeds.
hackathon_notes: pip install or the ZeroTouch installer; activity slowed since 2024, so check OpenTAKServer as a more active option.

name: OpenTAKServer
summary: Actively developed open-source TAK server for ATAK, iTAK and WinTAK with web UI, video streaming integration, Meshtastic support and certificate enrollment.
why_it_matters: Quick, modern backend for a common operating picture demo linking several sensors and phones.
hackathon_notes: Installer scripts for Linux/RPi; get clients connected in an hour, then focus on your sensor feed.

name: PyTAK
summary: Python asyncio package for TAK integration: CoT send/receive over TCP, UDP, TLS and multicast, with helpers for building events.
why_it_matters: The glue that turns any sensor script (GNSS monitor, Remote ID sniffer, DF array) into a TAK layer in a few lines.
hackathon_notes: pip install pytak; write a CoT generator for your detections. Lowest-friction way into the TAK ecosystem.

name: ADSBCOT
summary: Gateway that converts ADS-B traffic from dump1090/readsb or aggregator APIs into Cursor-on-Target so aircraft show in TAK.
why_it_matters: ADS-B also carries NIC/NACp integrity fields - the same signal GPSJam uses - so this is a ready bridge for a live GNSS-interference overlay.
hackathon_notes: Run alongside readsb on an RTL-SDR; add a filter that flags low NIC aircraft as an interference indicator.

name: readsb
summary: ADS-B/Mode S decoder for RTL-SDR and other receivers with networking, JSON output, MLAT support and aggregation features.
why_it_matters: Gives a team its own receiver for aircraft positions and navigation-integrity reports, the raw material for crowd-sourced jamming maps.
hackathon_notes: Install on a Pi with a cheap RTL-SDR and 1090 MHz antenna; JSON output is easy to parse for NIC/NACp statistics.

name: tar1090
summary: Improved web interface for readsb/dump1090 with track history, filtering and overlays.
why_it_matters: Ready-made visualization layer for an ADS-B based interference or airspace-awareness demo.
hackathon_notes: One-line install on top of readsb. Fork the JS to color aircraft by NIC to show degraded GNSS.

name: dump1090-fa
summary: FlightAware's maintained Mode S/ADS-B decoder for RTL-SDR dongles.
why_it_matters: Widely packaged alternative to readsb for the same ADS-B situational-awareness use.
hackathon_notes: apt-installable on Raspberry Pi OS; pick either this or readsb, not both.

name: OpenWebRX
summary: Multi-user web SDR receiver with waterfall display and many built-in digital decoders.
why_it_matters: Shared, browser-based spectrum view is a simple way to demonstrate RF situational awareness, e.g. watching the GNSS L1 band for interference with a suitable front end.
hackathon_notes: Docker image available. Upstream activity slowed after 2024; the luarvique fork is more active.

name: OpenWebRX+
summary: Actively developed fork of OpenWebRX adding decoders, bookmarks and packaging improvements.
why_it_matters: Same browser spectrum-monitoring capability with current maintenance.
hackathon_notes: Use the provided packages/Docker; works with RTL-SDR, Airspy, SDRplay, HackRF.

name: Gqrx
summary: Desktop SDR receiver built on GNU Radio and Qt with FFT/waterfall and demodulators.
why_it_matters: Quick local spectrum inspection when characterizing a jammer test signal in a shielded lab or checking band occupancy.
hackathon_notes: Available via brew/apt. Only transmit-free monitoring; never radiate in GNSS bands outside licensed test ranges.

name: KrakenSDR DoA DSP
summary: Direction-of-arrival processing and web UI for the five-channel coherent KrakenSDR, producing bearings to RF emitters.
why_it_matters: Passive DF of interference sources (or drone control links) is a core defensive-EW capability and maps well to a hackathon demo.
hackathon_notes: Needs KrakenSDR hardware (or recorded IQ). Prebuilt Raspberry Pi images exist (check the KrakenRF docs). Multiple stations plus Stone Soup gives triangulated emitter tracks.

name: Heimdall DAQ firmware
summary: Coherent multichannel SDR acquisition chain (sync, calibration, decimation) underneath KrakenSDR DoA and passive radar apps.
why_it_matters: Useful if you need raw coherent IQ for your own DF or interference-localization algorithm.
hackathon_notes: Installed as part of the KrakenSDR image; modify only if building custom DSP.

name: DroneSecurity (DJI DroneID receiver)
summary: Ruhr University Bochum receiver for DJI DroneID that works live with an SDR or offline on captures, released with their NDSS 2023 security analysis.
why_it_matters: Shows how passive decoding of drone telemetry supports detection and localization of DJI aircraft, a common C-UAS need.
hackathon_notes: Requires a wideband SDR (e.g. USRP/BladeRF) and recorded or live captures; sample captures ease offline work.

name: DragonSync
summary: Gateway that takes drone Remote ID / DroneID detections from WarDragon-style sensors and publishes them as CoT to TAK and other outputs.
why_it_matters: Working example of a passive drone-detection to common-operating-picture pipeline.
hackathon_notes: Read it as a reference architecture even without the WarDragon kit; reuse its CoT mapping for your own detector.

name: drone-mesh-mapper
summary: ESP32 firmware and tools that sniff Wi-Fi Remote ID and relay detections over Meshtastic LoRa mesh to a mapping host.
why_it_matters: Cheap, distributed, off-grid drone-awareness network - very hackathon friendly hardware.
hackathon_notes: ESP32 boards plus Meshtastic nodes cost little; flash and map in an afternoon.

name: MagNav challenge submission (lw-kong)
summary: A public submission repository for the JuliaCon 2020 MagNav signal-enhancement challenge, implementing a learned aircraft-field compensation.
why_it_matters: One of the few open challenge entries - shows what a competing compensation pipeline looks like end to end.
hackathon_notes: Inactive since 2022; useful as a template for a challenge-style submission on the MagNav data.

name: DARPA SubT Virtual Challenge
summary: Gazebo worlds, robot models, ROS interfaces and scoring tools from the virtual track of the DARPA Subterranean Challenge.
why_it_matters: Ready GNSS-denied underground environments with official scoring - a credible simulation testbed straight out of a DARPA challenge.
hackathon_notes: Dockerized, ROS1-era; heavy GPU/CPU needs. Use the hello-world repo as a starting point.

name: GBPlanner (CERBERUS)
summary: NTNU ARL graph-based exploration planner for subterranean environments, used in the DARPA SubT challenge on legged and aerial robots.
why_it_matters: Winning-team open code for autonomous exploration of GNSS-denied spaces with legged and aerial robots.
hackathon_notes: ROS1 catkin build with simulation demos; budget hours for dependencies. Pair with any lidar odometry.

name: MBPlanner
summary: Motion-primitive based exploration planner for fast aerial robots in confined spaces, used in CERBERUS flying platforms.
why_it_matters: Aerial complement to GBPlanner for drone exploration without GNSS.
hackathon_notes: ROS1, not updated since 2023.

name: LAMP (NeBula multi-robot SLAM)
summary: Team CoSTAR's large-scale multi-robot lidar SLAM back end with robust loop closure, from the NASA JPL-led SubT entry.
why_it_matters: Open component of the NeBula stack that won the SubT Urban circuit; shows multi-robot GNSS-denied mapping done at challenge scale.
hackathon_notes: ROS1 and dormant since 2023; run on the NeBula multi-robot dataset rather than live hardware.

name: NeBula multi-robot dataset
summary: Index for CoSTAR's multi-robot lidar/IMU/odometry datasets recorded in tunnels, mines and urban underground sites.
why_it_matters: Real GNSS-denied field data from SubT for testing SLAM or loop closure without building robots.
hackathon_notes: Bags are large; pick one sequence.

name: TARE Planner (CMU Explorer)
summary: Hierarchical exploration planner from CMU's Team Explorer, which earned the most-sectors-explored award at the SubT final.
why_it_matters: Well-documented, high-performing exploration planner that runs on top of a ready simulation stack.
hackathon_notes: Install the companion development environment first; ROS1 and ROS2 branches exist. Runs in sim on a laptop.

name: CMU Autonomous Exploration Development Environment
summary: CMU ground-robot development environment with simulated worlds, terrain analysis, local planner and waypoint tools used for exploration research (TARE, FAR planner).
why_it_matters: Fastest route to a GNSS-free autonomy demo: drop-in base for planners like TARE and FAR.
hackathon_notes: Download the Unity/Gazebo environment and run; the local planner and terrain analysis nodes are reusable standalone.

name: FAR Planner
summary: Visibility-graph route planner for known and unknown environments from the CMU SubT team.
why_it_matters: Long-range routing companion to exploration planners in GNSS-denied environments.
hackathon_notes: Runs in the same CMU development environment.

name: Time-optimal quadrotor planning
summary: Code for computing time-optimal quadrotor trajectories through waypoints, from the UZH group that placed second in AlphaPilot and built Swift.
why_it_matters: Insight into how top drone-racing teams plan; transferable to fast inspection or reconnaissance flight planning.
hackathon_notes: Python/CasADi, offline only. Inactive since 2021.

name: Flightmare
summary: Quadrotor simulator from UZH RPG with a decoupled Unity renderer and fast dynamics, aimed at RL and vision-based agile flight.
why_it_matters: Simulation lineage behind UZH's drone-racing work; useful for training vision-based navigation without hardware.
hackathon_notes: Last updated 2024 and ROS1-oriented; expect dependency fixing. Unity renderer binaries are separate downloads.

name: SPEED+ baseline
summary: PyTorch baselines and domain-bridging methods for spacecraft pose estimation on the SPEED+ dataset used in ESA Kelvins SPEC2021.
why_it_matters: Open code tied to an ESA competition on vision-based relative navigation and sim-to-real gap.
hackathon_notes: Dataset download is large; start with a subset. Inactive since 2023.

name: OpenCPN
summary: Cross-platform open-source chartplotter and navigation application that displays raster and S-57 vector charts, ingests GPS and AIS feeds, and runs waypoint routes. Large plugin ecosystem.
why_it_matters: The de facto open maritime nav display; a ready-made situational awareness front end for any surface-vessel or GNSS-denied maritime demo.
hackathon_notes: Install the packaged build, feed it NMEA over UDP/TCP from your own nav filter or a simulator and you have a chart display in minutes. Writing a plugin needs the plugin SDK and a full C++ build.

name: OpenCPN radar_pi
summary: OpenCPN plugin that connects to Navico and some Garmin and Raymarine marine radars and overlays radar imagery and ARPA-style targets on the chart.
why_it_matters: Shows how real marine radar returns are pulled into an open nav display, useful for radar-aided navigation and contact tracking demos.
hackathon_notes: Needs a supported radar on the network to be interesting; without hardware, study the protocol decoding and overlay code.

name: pyais
summary: Python library for decoding and encoding AIS NMEA sentences (AIVDM/AIVDO), including multi-part messages and streaming from sockets or files.
why_it_matters: The quickest path from raw AIS sentences to typed vessel positions for maritime picture building or AIS spoofing/anomaly detection.
hackathon_notes: pip install pyais, point it at a public AIS TCP feed or a recorded NMEA file, and you have vessel tracks in an hour. Pair with AIS-catcher for live RF.

name: noaadata
summary: Pure-Python AIS decode and encode library from a long-time AIS researcher, with message definitions and utilities for working with NOAA and coastal AIS data.
why_it_matters: A reference-quality alternative decoder, handy for cross-checking pyais output and for older message types.
hackathon_notes: Use mainly as a cross-check; pyais has the friendlier API.

name: AIS-catcher
summary: AIS receiver and decoder for cheap SDRs (RTL-SDR, Airspy, HackRF, SDRplay, SoapySDR) with a built-in web map, JSON/NMEA output and feed sharing.
why_it_matters: Turns a 30-dollar dongle into a live maritime picture sensor, the cheapest real RF input for a maritime awareness build.
hackathon_notes: Prebuilt binaries and Docker image; plug an RTL-SDR with a VHF antenna, run with the web viewer enabled, forward NMEA to pyais or OpenCPN. Inland sites may see few ships.

name: Signal K Server
summary: Node.js server implementing the Signal K open marine data standard: it ingests NMEA 0183, NMEA 2000 and other boat buses and republishes everything as a JSON data model over REST and WebSocket, with a plugin ecosystem.
why_it_matters: A modern data bus for a vessel; ideal glue between sensors, your own nav filter and displays.
hackathon_notes: Run via Docker or npm, enable the sample data playback, subscribe over WebSocket. Write a plugin to inject an alternative position source.

name: Signal K Specification
summary: The JSON schema and specification for the Signal K marine data format covering navigation, environment, propulsion and other vessel data paths.
why_it_matters: Gives a common vocabulary for maritime nav data instead of inventing one during a hackathon.
hackathon_notes: Read the navigation.* paths before designing your own message format.

name: signalk-to-nmea0183
summary: Signal K server plugin that converts Signal K data back into NMEA 0183 sentences for legacy displays and autopilots.
why_it_matters: Lets a custom position or heading source reach any off-the-shelf NMEA consumer such as OpenCPN or a chartplotter.
hackathon_notes: Enable in the Signal K admin UI, choose sentences, output over TCP.

name: MOOS-IvP
summary: Long-running autonomy middleware (MOOS) plus the IvP Helm behaviour-based multi-objective decision engine, used widely for autonomous marine vehicles, including COLREGs-aware collision avoidance behaviours.
why_it_matters: The academic and navy-adjacent reference for marine vehicle autonomy; much published USV/UUV collision avoidance work is built on it.
hackathon_notes: Builds on Linux/macOS with CMake; the bundled alpha and heron missions run in simulation with pMarineViewer. Pair with the MIT 2.680 labs.

name: MOOS-IvP COLREGs master's research code
summary: MOOS-IvP applications from a 2025 master's project at Universidade de Sao Paulo implementing COLREGs-compliant collision avoidance for USVs, including a modified A* planner, a velocity-obstacle method and a virtual-contact spawner for test encounters.
why_it_matters: Recent, field-validated COLREGs avoidance code that plugs straight into MOOS-IvP.
hackathon_notes: Build against a MOOS-IvP tree; use pContactSpawn to stage head-on/crossing/overtaking cases.

name: NTNU colav-simulator
summary: Python framework from the NTNU Autoship centre for simulating and evaluating autonomous ship collision avoidance controllers, open-sourced in autumn 2025, with scenario generation and evaluation tooling.
why_it_matters: One of the few open, evaluation-oriented COLAV simulators from a leading autonomous ship lab; good test bench for COLREGs logic.
hackathon_notes: Python with uv; define scenarios and swap in your own planner. Pair with its VIMMJIPDA tracker for realistic target estimates.

name: VIMMJIPDA tracker interface
summary: Interface that runs the VIMMJIPDA multi-target tracker (visibility, interacting multiple models, JIPDA) inside the NTNU colav-simulator; open-sourced November 2025.
why_it_matters: A maritime-grade multi-target tracker connected to a collision avoidance loop, closing the sense-track-avoid chain.
hackathon_notes: Install with uv alongside colav-simulator; the core tracker code itself lives on Code Ocean.

name: Aeolus Ocean
summary: Collision avoidance simulator for COLREG-compliant autonomous ship navigation intended for use as a digital twin under varied weather and day/night conditions.
why_it_matters: Another research testbed for COLREGs logic with environmental variation.
hackathon_notes: Little recent activity; check the README for build steps before committing time.

name: Virtual RobotX (VRX)
summary: Gazebo-based simulation environment for the RobotX maritime autonomy competition, with a WAM-V USV model, waves, wind, sensors and scored tasks such as station keeping, wayfinding and perception.
why_it_matters: Ready-made surface-vessel sim with nav and perception tasks; good for maritime autonomy demos.
hackathon_notes: Current branch targets gz-sim and ROS 2. Task worlds (station keeping, wayfinding) work as hackathon challenges out of the box.

name: Water Linked DVL Python
summary: Example Python code for talking to Water Linked DVLs over their serial and TCP/JSON protocols, parsing velocity and dead-reckoning reports.
why_it_matters: DVL velocity is the core GNSS-free aid for underwater dead reckoning; this is the shortest route to real DVL data.
hackathon_notes: Needs a DVL or recorded JSON; protocol is simple JSON over TCP so a replay mock is easy.

name: Water Linked DVL A50 ROS driver
summary: ROS 1 driver publishing Water Linked DVL A50 velocity and beam data as ROS messages; now archived.
why_it_matters: Reference ROS integration for DVL-aided navigation.
hackathon_notes: Archived; port the parsing to ROS 2 or use dvl-python directly.

name: Ping Python
summary: Python library and examples for Blue Robotics Ping echosounder and Ping360 scanning sonar using the Ping protocol.
why_it_matters: Cheap altimeter and sonar input for underwater navigation and obstacle sensing.
hackathon_notes: pip install bluerobotics-ping; requires the hardware or Ping Viewer logs.

name: Ping Viewer
summary: Desktop application to view and record data from Blue Robotics Ping echosounder and Ping360 sonar.
why_it_matters: Fast way to record sonar logs for offline SLAM or odometry experiments.
hackathon_notes: Prebuilt releases; logs can be replayed into ping-python.

name: ping360_sonar ROS package
summary: ROS package that drives the Ping360 scanning sonar and publishes scans as images and laser-scan style messages.
why_it_matters: Gets low-cost scanning sonar into a ROS SLAM or obstacle pipeline.
hackathon_notes: Needs the sonar; the laser-scan output plugs into standard 2D SLAM tools.

name: Project DAVE
summary: Gazebo-based underwater simulation environment from the Naval Postgraduate School and partners, extending UUV Simulator with DVL, sonar, bathymetry and manipulation models.
why_it_matters: Navy-funded underwater sim with realistic DVL and sonar sensors for testing AUV nav without water.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1 Noetic + Gazebo 11 via Docker; setup is heavy, budget half a day. A ROS 2 port has been in progress.

name: NPS underwater multibeam sonar plugin
summary: GPU (CUDA) multibeam sonar simulation plugin for Gazebo producing physically motivated sonar imagery.
why_it_matters: Synthetic sonar data for testing sonar odometry and SLAM.
hackathon_notes: Needs an NVIDIA GPU; used within DAVE.

name: UUV Simulator
summary: Gazebo/ROS packages for underwater vehicle simulation with hydrodynamics, thrusters and sensors; archived.
why_it_matters: Many underwater-nav papers and DAVE build on it; useful for reference models.
hackathon_notes: Archived and tied to old ROS/Gazebo; use Stonefish or DAVE instead.

name: Stonefish
summary: C++ simulation library for marine robotics with hydrodynamics, underwater rendering and sensors including DVL, USBL, multibeam and forward-looking sonar; has a ROS wrapper.
why_it_matters: One of the few open sims with credible underwater nav sensors for AUV dead reckoning and sonar-based localization work.
hackathon_notes: Build with CMake; use stonefish_ros for ROS integration. Good for a DVL+USBL EKF demo.

name: HoloOcean ROS bridge
summary: ROS bridge for HoloOcean, BYU's Unreal Engine based underwater simulator with DVL, IMU, depth, sonar and acoustic modem sensors.
why_it_matters: Photo-realistic underwater sim with multi-agent acoustic comms, useful for cooperative AUV nav.
hackathon_notes: HoloOcean itself is installed via pip plus a large world package; the bridge adds ROS topics. Needs a decent GPU.

name: USBL Simulator
summary: C++ library and ROS 2 node that simulates ultra-short baseline acoustic positioning measurements, with a Gazebo plugin.
why_it_matters: USBL is the main absolute fix for submerged vehicles; simulated USBL lets a team test an aided-INS filter.
hackathon_notes: ROS 2 colcon build; generate USBL fixes to fuse with DVL dead reckoning.

name: AuvEstimator
summary: Work-in-progress EKF that fuses DVL, IMU and barometer data for AUV state estimation, with a ROS wrapper.
why_it_matters: Small, readable DVL-aided INS example to start a GNSS-free underwater nav filter from.
hackathon_notes: Dormant since 2021; treat as a starting template, not a dependency.

name: SMARC navigation
summary: Localization and SLAM components for the SMARC AUVs (KTH), including EKF localization with IMU, DVL and multibeam sonar against a feature map.
why_it_matters: Research AUV navigation from a Swedish maritime robotics centre, showing map-aided underwater localization.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1 era and dormant; read for architecture.

name: sonar-SLAM
summary: Underwater SLAM for robots with multibeam imaging sonar, from Stevens Institute research on BlueROV-class vehicles, combining sonar feature extraction and pose-graph optimization.
why_it_matters: One of the more complete open sonar SLAM pipelines; directly relevant to GNSS-free underwater navigation.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1 with sample bags; budget time for dependencies.

name: BRUCE
summary: BlueROV underwater SLAM and exploration code from Stevens Institute, combining sonar-based SLAM with active exploration planning.
why_it_matters: Predecessor to sonar-SLAM; shows SLAM-driven exploration underwater.
hackathon_notes: Dormant since 2020.

name: DISO
summary: Direct imaging sonar odometry: estimates vehicle motion directly from forward-looking imaging sonar frames without feature extraction.
why_it_matters: Sonar odometry is a key aid when DVL bottom-lock or vision fails in turbid water.
hackathon_notes: C++ with ROS; try on the provided datasets first.

name: Vortex AUV
summary: Guidance, navigation and control software from NTNU's student Vortex team for competition AUVs and ROVs, built on ROS 2.
why_it_matters: A complete, actively maintained student AUV GNC stack to borrow structure from.
hackathon_notes: ROS 2 workspace; sim integration via their companion repos.

name: Autoware
summary: Meta-repository for Autoware, the open-source ROS 2 autonomous driving stack covering localization (NDT, EKF), perception, planning and control.
why_it_matters: The biggest open ground-vehicle autonomy stack; its localization modules are a mature map-based alternative when GNSS is degraded.
hackathon_notes: Heavy: use the Docker images and the planning simulator. For a hackathon, lift single packages such as NDT scan matcher or the EKF localizer.

name: Autoware Universe
summary: The broad package collection of Autoware with experimental and production-candidate modules, including localization, pose initialization and GNSS/IMU fusion.
why_it_matters: Where most Autoware localization code actually lives.
hackathon_notes: Pick packages like autoware_ndt_scan_matcher and autoware_ekf_localizer and run them standalone with rosbags.

name: AWSIM
summary: Unity-based digital-twin simulator for Autoware with simulated lidar, camera, GNSS and IMU.
why_it_matters: Lets a team exercise Autoware localization without a car.
hackathon_notes: Prebuilt binaries for Ubuntu with an NVIDIA GPU.

name: Baidu Apollo
summary: Baidu's open autonomous driving platform, including the multi-sensor fusion localization module combining GNSS RTK, IMU and lidar map matching.
why_it_matters: Its MSF localization design is a well-documented reference for GNSS/INS/lidar fusion in vehicles.
hackathon_notes: Very heavy to build; read the localization module docs and code rather than deploy.

name: grid_map
summary: C++ library and ROS integration for multi-layer 2.5D grid maps, widely used for elevation and traversability mapping.
why_it_matters: Standard data structure for terrain-aware off-road navigation.
hackathon_notes: apt install ros-<distro>-grid-map; convert DEMs or point clouds to layers quickly.

name: elevation_mapping
summary: ETH Zurich robot-centric elevation mapping for rough terrain navigation that fuses range data into a probabilistic 2.5D map.
why_it_matters: Classic baseline for terrain mapping on legged and wheeled robots.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1 and dormant since 2022; prefer the GPU version.

name: elevation_mapping_cupy
