summary: GNSS/INS/Camera integrated navigation library supporting a range of GNSS modes (SPP, RTK, PPP and variants) tightly fused with inertial and visual data via factor graph optimization.
why_it_matters: One of the most complete open tightly coupled GNSS/INS/vision stacks; good for showing positioning robustness in degraded GNSS.
hackathon_notes: Large codebase; run on the provided dataset first. Config files are the main interface.

name: GLIO
summary: Tightly coupled GNSS/LiDAR/IMU integration (PolyU) for continuous, drift-free state estimation in urban canyons.
why_it_matters: Shows how raw GNSS measurements can be kept in the loop even when only a few satellites are visible.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1 research code; needs raw GNSS observables in the data.

name: pyins
summary: Python package for modelling and analysing inertial navigation systems: strapdown integration, error models, Kalman-filter aiding and sensor simulation.
why_it_matters: Pure-Python INS/GNSS playground for quick outage and sensor-grade studies.
hackathon_notes: pip-installable with docs on readthedocs. Good for scripted what-if plots (tactical vs MEMS IMU drift).

name: strapdown-rs
summary: Rust implementation of a strapdown inertial navigation system, aimed at simulation and research on INS behaviour.
why_it_matters: Lesser-known, actively developed Rust INS; memory-safe option for embedded or simulation pipelines.
hackathon_notes: cargo build; small and readable. Check the crate docs for current API.

name: ESKF (je310)
summary: Error-state Kalman filter implementation following Sola's quaternion ESKF formulation.
why_it_matters: Compact code reference for Sola's equations when writing your own ESKF.
hackathon_notes: Small codebase, no recent updates; read alongside the Sola report.

name: ESKF ROS (EliaTarasov)
summary: ROS error-state Kalman filter derived from PX4/ecl that fuses IMU with GPS, magnetometer, vision pose and optical flow.
why_it_matters: PX4-style estimator outside the autopilot, easy to feed from a bag.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1, unmaintained since 2019.

name: imu_gps_localization
summary: Error-state Kalman filter fusing IMU and GPS for localization, small and readable.
why_it_matters: Minimal ESKF GNSS/IMU example good for a first hackathon filter.
hackathon_notes: Small ROS project; easy to strip ROS and port.

name: eskf-gps-imu-fusion
summary: ESKF fusing GPS and IMU for improved positioning, with documentation in Chinese.
why_it_matters: Another compact ESKF reference with a worked dataset.
hackathon_notes: Standalone CMake build; docs are in Chinese.

name: imu_x_fusion
summary: Loosely coupled IMU + GNSS / 6-DoF odometry fusion with multiple estimators side by side (ESKF, IEKF, UKF variants, MAP).
why_it_matters: Lets you compare filter variants on the same inputs with little code.
hackathon_notes: ROS package; swap estimator by config to compare behaviour.

name: gps_imu_fusion
summary: GPS/IMU fusion examples implemented with ESKF, EKF, UKF and other filters.
why_it_matters: Small comparison set of filter types for GNSS/IMU.
hackathon_notes: Inactive since 2022; use as reading material.

name: invariant-ekf (Hartley InEKF)
summary: C++ library implementing the invariant EKF for aided inertial navigation, including contact-aided legged-robot state estimation.
why_it_matters: Reference InEKF implementation; invariant filters behave better than standard EKF under large initial errors.
hackathon_notes: Last push 2019; still compiles with Eigen. Pairs with the Hartley 2019 paper.

name: DRIFT
summary: Symmetry-preserving (invariant) state estimation library from University of Michigan for legged, wheeled and other robots, with real-time ROS support.
why_it_matters: Maintained InEKF stack for proprioceptive dead reckoning when GNSS and vision are unavailable.
hackathon_notes: Has ROS examples; try on a wheeled robot bag for GNSS-free odometry.

name: iekf (contagon)
summary: Invariant Kalman filter implementation on SE(2) and SE(3).
why_it_matters: Small Python-side InEKF example for learning.
hackathon_notes: Small research repo; use for learning the algorithm.

name: gnss-ins-sim
summary: Python GNSS/INS simulator that generates trajectories, IMU/GNSS/magnetometer measurements with configurable error models, and runs navigation algorithms on them.
why_it_matters: Quick way to produce synthetic IMU and GNSS data with known truth to test filters and dead reckoning under GNSS outage.
hackathon_notes: Pure Python; define a motion profile CSV and sensor grade, then plug your filter in as an algorithm.

name: allan_variance_ros
summary: ROS tool (Oxford DRS) that computes Allan deviation plots from an IMU bag and outputs noise parameters in a Kalibr-compatible format.
why_it_matters: Needed to get realistic IMU noise values for any filter or VIO setup.
hackathon_notes: Record a few hours of static IMU data before the event; the analysis itself is quick.

name: imu_utils
summary: ROS package for analysing IMU performance with Allan variance to estimate noise and bias instability.
why_it_matters: Common alternative to allan_variance_ros in VIO workflows.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1, depends on Ceres; needs long static logs.

name: kalibr_allan (archived)
summary: MATLAB scripts producing IMU Allan standard deviation charts and Kalibr-ready noise values.
why_it_matters: Historical reference for IMU noise characterisation.
hackathon_notes: Archived; prefer allan_variance_ros.

name: allan-variance (Python)
summary: Small Python package computing Allan variance and fitting standard noise parameters.
why_it_matters: Quick no-ROS Allan analysis in a notebook.
hackathon_notes: pip install; feed a numpy array of static IMU samples.

name: AV-Matlab-SW
summary: MATLAB software for Allan variance calculations accompanying a published article on IMU noise characterisation (Farrell et al.).
why_it_matters: Deeper treatment of Allan variance pitfalls than the typical tool.
hackathon_notes: Read with the paper; MATLAB required.

name: Kalibr
summary: ETH ASL calibration toolbox for multi-camera and camera-IMU systems (extrinsics and time offset), plus IMU intrinsics and rolling-shutter calibration.
why_it_matters: Standard way to calibrate a camera-IMU rig before running any VIO.
hackathon_notes: Use the Docker image to avoid ROS 1 build pain; print an AprilGrid target in advance.

name: iKalibr
summary: Continuous-time, targetless multi-sensor calibration framework (IMU, cameras, LiDAR, radar, RGB-D, event cameras) estimating extrinsics and time offsets (IEEE T-RO 2025).
why_it_matters: Calibrate a full heterogeneous rig, including radar, in one tool.
hackathon_notes: ROS-based with many dependencies; budget setup time.

name: imu_tk
summary: Tool for calibrating IMU intrinsics (misalignment, scale factors and biases of accelerometer and gyro) from a sequence of static poses, without a turntable.
why_it_matters: Cheap way to improve MEMS IMU accuracy before deploying a filter.
hackathon_notes: Needs Ceres; collect static poses in many orientations with short rotations between.

name: lidar_imu_calib
summary: Automatic calibration of the extrinsic rotation between a 3D LiDAR and an IMU.
why_it_matters: Quick LiDAR-IMU rotation estimate for LIO setups.
hackathon_notes: Inactive since 2021; rotation only.

name: LI-Calib
summary: Targetless LiDAR-IMU calibration based on continuous-time batch estimation (IROS 2020).
why_it_matters: Full LiDAR-IMU extrinsics without a target.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1; needs a sequence with rich excitation.

name: LiDAR_IMU_Init
summary: Real-time LiDAR-inertial initialization estimating extrinsics, time offset, gravity and IMU bias online (IROS 2022).
why_it_matters: Removes the extrinsic-calibration blocker when bolting a LiDAR and IMU onto a new platform.
hackathon_notes: Builds like FAST_LIO; feed a bag with aggressive motion at start.

name: AHRS (Python)
summary: Python collection of attitude estimation algorithms (Madgwick, Mahony, complementary, EKF, QUEST, TRIAD and more) plus utilities such as the World Magnetic Model and WGS84.
why_it_matters: One import to compare attitude filters on your IMU log.
hackathon_notes: pip install ahrs; numpy arrays in, quaternions out.

name: x-io Fusion
summary: x-io Technologies' C AHRS library (revised Madgwick-style algorithm) with gyro offset correction, acceleration and magnetic disturbance rejection, and Python bindings.
why_it_matters: Production-grade embedded attitude filter with disturbance rejection, from the Madgwick filter's originators.
hackathon_notes: Drop the C files into firmware or pip install imufusion for Python prototyping.

name: MadgwickAHRS (Arduino)
summary: Official Arduino library implementing the Madgwick AHRS filter.
why_it_matters: Fastest hardware demo of attitude estimation on a microcontroller.
hackathon_notes: Install from the Arduino library manager; set sample rate correctly.

name: madgwick_py
summary: Minimal Python implementation of Madgwick's IMU and AHRS algorithms.
why_it_matters: Readable algorithm reference.
hackathon_notes: Tiny, unmaintained; use for reading.

name: imu_tools
summary: ROS tools for IMUs: Madgwick and complementary orientation filters and an RViz IMU visualisation plugin.
why_it_matters: Standard ROS orientation filter feeding robot_localization.
hackathon_notes: apt install on ROS 2.

name: ZUPT-aided INS (OpenShoe MATLAB)
summary: MATLAB implementation of the OpenShoe zero-velocity-aided foot-mounted INS with several zero-velocity detectors (SHOE, acceleration variance and magnitude, angular rate energy).
why_it_matters: Reference for dismounted soldier / first responder navigation without GNSS.
hackathon_notes: Works with any foot-mounted IMU log; sample data included. No updates since 2021.

name: PyShoe
summary: Open Python foot-mounted INS from UTIAS with a public inertial dataset and several zero-velocity detectors, including learned ones.
why_it_matters: Ready-to-run dismounted navigation pipeline with data for evaluation.
hackathon_notes: Python; dataset download needed. Strap an IMU to a boot and compare detectors.

name: RoNIN
summary: Robust Neural Inertial Navigation: smartphone IMU dataset and baseline networks (ResNet, LSTM, TCN) regressing pedestrian velocity from IMU.
why_it_matters: Main benchmark and baselines for learned pedestrian inertial navigation.
hackathon_notes: PyTorch; dataset is large. Pretrained models give a quick baseline.

name: TLIO
summary: Tight Learned Inertial Odometry: a network regresses displacement and uncertainty from IMU windows, fused in a stochastic-cloning EKF.
why_it_matters: Strong blueprint for combining a learned motion prior with a classical filter.
hackathon_notes: Training data is head-mounted; expect domain gap on other platforms.

name: AI-IMU Dead-Reckoning
summary: Car dead reckoning from IMU only, using an invariant EKF whose noise covariances are adapted by a neural network, evaluated on KITTI.
why_it_matters: Ground vehicle navigation through GNSS outages using only the IMU.
hackathon_notes: PyTorch; KITTI raw data needed. Clear demo of IMU-only drift reduction.

name: Denoise IMU Gyro
summary: CNN that denoises low-cost gyroscope signals to improve attitude estimation.
why_it_matters: Shows learned correction for cheap MEMS gyros.
hackathon_notes: Inactive since 2020; trained on EuRoC/TUM-VI.

name: AirIMU
summary: Learns IMU error correction and uncertainty with a network, combined with differentiable IMU preintegration (CMU AirLab).
why_it_matters: Learned IMU correction that feeds uncertainty into classical estimators.
hackathon_notes: PyTorch and PyPose; pretrained models available.

name: AirIO
summary: Learning-based inertial odometry for UAVs that improves feature observability by changing the IMU data representation (IEEE RA-L 2025).
why_it_matters: Recent IMU-only drone odometry for GNSS-denied flight.
hackathon_notes: Recent research code; check README for datasets.

name: EqNIO
summary: Subequivariant neural inertial odometry (ICLR 2025) that canonicalises IMU data so networks generalise across orientations; applied on top of TLIO and RoNIN.
why_it_matters: State of the art learned inertial odometry with released code.
hackathon_notes: Builds on TLIO/RoNIN pipelines; set those up first.

name: Learned Inertial Odometry for Drone Racing
summary: UZH RPG code fusing a learned inertial displacement model with an EKF for drone racing state estimation.
why_it_matters: Shows learned IO on aggressive UAV flight.
hackathon_notes: Research code; datasets from UZH.

name: manif
summary: Header-only C++11 library for Lie theory (SO2, SE2, SO3, SE3, SE_2(3) and more) with Jacobians, built around Sola's micro Lie theory paper; Python bindings available.
why_it_matters: Correct on-manifold Jacobians for custom ESKF or factor-graph code.
hackathon_notes: Header-only; Python bindings via pip/conda. Use alongside the micro Lie theory paper.

name: Sophus
summary: C++ Lie group library (SO2, SE2, SO3, SE3, Sim3) built on Eigen, used in many SLAM and VIO systems.
why_it_matters: De facto Lie group dependency in SLAM codebases.
hackathon_notes: Header-mostly; widely packaged.

name: liegroups (Python)
summary: Python implementation of SO2, SE2, SO3 and SE3 matrix Lie groups with numpy and PyTorch backends.
why_it_matters: Lie group operations inside PyTorch for learned estimators.
hackathon_notes: pip install from source; small and stable.

name: navlie
summary: Python state estimation package on Lie groups (McGill DECAR): EKF, iterated EKF, sigma-point filters, batch estimation, and IMU kinematics models.
why_it_matters: Fastest way to prototype on-manifold INS filters in Python.
hackathon_notes: pip install; has IMU and GNSS-like examples.

name: Nav2 (ROS 2 Navigation)
summary: The standard ROS 2 navigation stack: behavior-tree driven navigator, global planners (NavFn, Smac hybrid-A*/lattice, Theta*), local controllers (DWB, MPPI, Regulated Pure Pursuit), costmaps, recovery behaviors and waypoint following, including GPS waypoints via robot_localization.
why_it_matters: Default autonomy layer for ground robots in ROS 2; the place to plug a GNSS-denied localization source and still get full point-to-point and waypoint missions.
hackathon_notes: apt install ros-<distro>-navigation2 plus nav2_bringup gives a Gazebo TurtleBot demo in under an hour. Swap AMCL for your own localization by publishing map->odom TF. Tuning params YAML is the main time sink.

name: opennav_coverage
summary: Nav2-compatible complete-coverage task server and navigator built on Fields2Cover, with behavior-tree utilities for field/area coverage and row following.
why_it_matters: Gives Nav2 robots area-search and survey patterns (boustrophedon sweeps over a polygon) out of the box, useful for search, mapping and route clearance scenarios.
hackathon_notes: Needs a source build of Fields2Cover; send a polygon in GPS or map frame and get a coverage route. Best for flat open terrain.

name: OMPL - Open Motion Planning Library
summary: Library of sampling-based motion planners (RRT, RRT*, PRM, BIT*, informed variants, kinodynamic planners) with a clean state-space abstraction and Python bindings.
why_it_matters: The reference implementation for sampling-based planning; underpins MoveIt and many UAV/UGV planners, so it is the quickest way to get a correct baseline planner.
hackathon_notes: pip wheels exist for the Python bindings; define a state validity checker against your occupancy grid or DEM and you have a planner in an afternoon.

name: EGO-Planner
summary: ESDF-free gradient-based local planner for quadrotors from ZJU FAST Lab: optimizes B-spline trajectories using collision terms computed only where the trajectory hits obstacles.
why_it_matters: Lightweight onboard replanning for small drones flying through clutter; widely reused baseline for agile UAV navigation in unknown environments.
hackathon_notes: ROS1 (Noetic) with a bundled simulator; runs on a laptop. Porting to ROS 2 / PX4 needs a bridge. Good for a demo of reactive flight in a random forest map.

name: Fast-Planner
summary: HKUST quadrotor planning framework: kinodynamic A* front-end plus B-spline optimization, with topological and perception-aware variants for fast flight in unknown environments.
why_it_matters: Classic baseline that most later UAV planners compare against; modular enough to reuse its mapping (ESDF) and search components.
hackathon_notes: ROS1 + Gazebo-free lightweight sim; builds in minutes on Ubuntu 20.04. Expect NLopt dependency friction.

name: FUEL - Fast UAV Exploration
summary: Frontier-information-structure based autonomous exploration for quadrotors, combining global tour planning over frontiers with local viewpoint refinement.
why_it_matters: Autonomous mapping of unknown buildings or terrain without GNSS or prior map, a core reconnaissance capability.
hackathon_notes: Bundled sim; pairs naturally with a VIO/LiDAR odometry source from other lanes.

name: RACER - multi-UAV exploration
summary: Rapid collaborative exploration with multiple UAVs: decomposes unknown space and allocates exploration regions between drones with pairwise communication.
why_it_matters: A worked example of multi-robot task allocation for exploration under limited comms.
hackathon_notes: Same toolchain as FUEL; run 2-4 drones in sim and vary comm range.

name: GCOPTER
summary: General-purpose multicopter trajectory optimizer (MINCO) handling safe-corridor constraints and dynamic limits with spatial-temporal deformation.
why_it_matters: Efficient, well-documented trajectory optimizer to turn waypoint paths into flyable minimum-control trajectories.
hackathon_notes: Header-heavy C++ with ROS1 examples; best used as a library behind your own front-end.

name: KR Autonomous Flight
summary: UPenn Kumar Robotics end-to-end autonomy stack for GPS-denied quadrotors: state estimation, mapping, planning and control in one system.
why_it_matters: Full reference stack for flying without GNSS in forests and under canopy, from a lab with many field deployments.
hackathon_notes: Docker images help; large build. Use it to see how estimation and planning are glued, or reuse the planner.

name: MADER
summary: MIT ACL decentralized and asynchronous trajectory planner for multiple UAVs in dynamic environments with obstacle and agent avoidance.
why_it_matters: Multi-agent planning without synchronized clocks or central coordination, closer to real comms constraints.
hackathon_notes: No commits since 2022; ROS1. Use for ideas rather than code reuse.

name: PlanSys2
summary: PDDL-based symbolic planning system for ROS 2: domain/problem management, plan generation with off-the-shelf planners and execution via behavior trees.
why_it_matters: Turns high-level mission goals (visit, inspect, deliver) into executable action sequences, the missing layer above Nav2.
hackathon_notes: apt-installable; write a PDDL domain and wrap Nav2 goals as actions. Learning PDDL is the time cost.

name: BehaviorTree.CPP
summary: C++ behavior tree library with XML trees, async actions, logging and the Groot editor; the execution engine inside Nav2 and many mission frameworks.
why_it_matters: Standard way to compose navigation, fallback and recovery logic into readable mission trees.
hackathon_notes: Header-friendly library; Groot2 GUI helps demo mission logic to judges.

name: PythonRobotics
summary: Large collection of readable Python implementations of robotics algorithms: localization (EKF, particle filter), SLAM, path planning (A*, RRT*, D*, state lattice), path tracking and more, with animations.
why_it_matters: Best teaching and prototyping resource; copy a planner or filter into a hackathon prototype in minutes.
hackathon_notes: Pure numpy/matplotlib; no build. Good for a quick 2D planner over a rasterized DEM.

name: Fields2Cover
summary: Modular coverage path planning library: headland generation, swath generation, route ordering (boustrophedon, snake, spiral) and Dubins/Reeds-Shepp path smoothing, with Python bindings.
why_it_matters: Ready coverage planner for area search or survey patterns by ground or air vehicles.
hackathon_notes: Build from source with GDAL dependency; Python bindings let you produce a sweep over a GeoJSON polygon quickly.

name: polygon_coverage_planning
summary: ETH ASL coverage planner for polygons with holes that treats boustrophedon sweep selection as a generalized TSP, aimed at UAV survey.
why_it_matters: Handles no-fly holes inside a survey area, which simple lawnmower generators do not.
hackathon_notes: ROS1 + CGAL; last push 2023. Use as a reference or run offline to produce waypoint lists.

name: grid_map
summary: Universal multi-layer 2.5D grid map library for mobile robots with ROS/ROS 2 integration, filters, iterators and conversion to images, point clouds and costmaps.
why_it_matters: Common data structure for elevation, slope and cost layers - the glue between DEMs and planners.
hackathon_notes: Available as ROS 2 binaries; load a GeoTIFF DEM (via GDAL) into a grid_map layer for terrain-aware costs.

name: Spatio-Temporal Voxel Layer
summary: Nav2 costmap layer using OpenVDB voxel grids with time decay to represent 3D obstacles from depth and LiDAR sensors.
why_it_matters: Better 3D obstacle handling for ground robots in dynamic environments than the default voxel layer.
hackathon_notes: Drop-in Nav2 plugin via apt.

name: CBBA (Python)
summary: Python implementation of the Consensus-Based Bundle Algorithm for decentralized multi-agent task allocation with plotting examples.
why_it_matters: CBBA is the classic decentralized auction for assigning tasks to UAV teams; this is an easy-to-read starting point.
hackathon_notes: numpy + matplotlib only; wrap in a ROS 2 node or call from a mission script to assign search cells to drones.

name: Open-RMF rmf_task
summary: Task allocation library from Open-RMF that assigns tasks to fleets of robots, accounting for battery, travel time and task constraints.
why_it_matters: Production-grade multi-robot task allocation with a fleet-level view, transferable from logistics to multi-vehicle missions.
hackathon_notes: Part of the larger Open-RMF stack; worth it only if you want fleet management, otherwise use CBBA.

name: GDAL
summary: Translator library and CLI tools for raster and vector geospatial formats (GeoTIFF, COG, GeoPackage, Shapefile, KML and hundreds more) with reprojection, warping and DEM utilities.
why_it_matters: Every map, DEM and imagery pipeline goes through GDAL; gdalwarp, gdaldem and gdal_translate cover most reference-map preparation.
hackathon_notes: Use conda or the OSGeo Docker image to avoid version mismatches between GDAL and Python bindings.

name: PROJ
summary: Cartographic projection and coordinate transformation library with datum grids, time-dependent transformations and a pipeline syntax.
why_it_matters: Correct datum and projection handling (WGS84, ITRF, local grids, UTM) is foundational for any nav system that mixes map sources.
hackathon_notes: Bundle the proj-data grids offline if your demo has no internet.

name: pyproj
summary: Python interface to PROJ for CRS definitions, coordinate transformations and geodesic computations.
why_it_matters: Default Python tool for lat/lon <-> UTM/ECEF/local conversions in nav prototypes.
hackathon_notes: pip install pyproj ships PROJ inside the wheel; reuse a Transformer object for speed.

name: Rasterio
summary: Pythonic raster I/O on top of GDAL: read/write GeoTIFF and COG, windowed reads, masks and affine georeferencing.
why_it_matters: Easiest way to sample a DEM or orthophoto at a coordinate for terrain-referenced or visual navigation experiments.
hackathon_notes: pip wheels include GDAL; use windowed reads to crop tiles around a vehicle position.

name: QGIS
summary: Desktop open-source GIS for viewing, editing, analyzing and printing geospatial data, extensible via Python plugins.
why_it_matters: The analyst's workbench for building mission areas, inspecting DEMs and checking flight logs on a map.
hackathon_notes: Install the LTR build; draw AOIs and export GeoJSON for planners. QGIS loads MBTiles/PMTiles for offline basemaps.

name: CesiumJS
summary: WebGL 3D globe and map library with terrain, 3D Tiles, time-dynamic data (CZML) and accurate WGS84 rendering.
why_it_matters: Best open web option for a 3D situational awareness view with terrain and flight paths; widely used in defense demos.
hackathon_notes: npm install cesium. Default imagery/terrain use Cesium ion (token); for offline, serve your own quantized-mesh terrain and tiles.

name: Cesium Terrain Builder
summary: Command-line tools to convert GDAL-readable DEMs into Cesium terrain tiles (heightmap and quantized-mesh with the docker variant).
why_it_matters: Turns a Copernicus/SRTM DEM into offline 3D terrain for a CesiumJS display without internet.
hackathon_notes: Unmaintained since 2023; use the tum-gis docker image to avoid build pain.

name: MapLibre GL JS
summary: Open-source WebGL vector tile map renderer (fork of Mapbox GL JS v1) with styles, 3D terrain and globe view.
why_it_matters: Fast, license-clean 2D/2.5D web map for C2 dashboards, works fully offline with your own tiles.
hackathon_notes: Pair with martin or tileserver-gl and a PMTiles extract for an offline basemap.

name: OpenLayers
summary: Feature-rich web mapping library supporting many projections, WMS/WMTS, vector tiles and editing.
why_it_matters: Strong choice when you need non-Web-Mercator projections or OGC services in a C2 web UI.
hackathon_notes: npm install ol; integrates with proj4js for custom CRS.

name: Leaflet
summary: Small, simple JavaScript library for interactive raster/vector maps with a huge plugin ecosystem.
why_it_matters: Quickest route to a working map with markers and tracks in a hackathon UI.
hackathon_notes: Works with milsymbol to render unit icons as markers.

name: deck.gl
summary: GPU-powered large-scale data visualization framework with layers for points, paths, trips, hexbins and 3D tiles, usable over MapLibre or standalone.
why_it_matters: Renders thousands of tracks (ADS-B, AIS, swarm telemetry) smoothly for a common operating picture.
hackathon_notes: Use TripsLayer for animated track histories; integrates with React.

name: OSRM
summary: High-performance road routing engine on OpenStreetMap data using contraction hierarchies or multi-level Dijkstra.
why_it_matters: Offline road routing for ground vehicle convoy and logistics planning.
hackathon_notes: Docker image + a Geofabrik regional extract gives a routing API in under an hour.

name: Valhalla
summary: Tiled OSM routing engine with dynamic costing per request (auto, truck, pedestrian, bicycle), isochrones and map matching.
why_it_matters: Request-time costing makes it easy to avoid areas or prefer terrain types, and its map-matching snaps noisy tracks to roads.
hackathon_notes: Docker images available; build tiles for a region once and run offline. Elevation tiles enable grade-aware costing.

name: GraphHopper
summary: Java OSM routing engine usable as library or server, with custom models for per-request costing and map matching.
why_it_matters: Embeddable routing on JVM/Android, relevant for on-device dismounted navigation apps.
hackathon_notes: Single jar + OSM pbf; custom model JSON lets you penalize road classes or areas.

name: OSMnx
summary: Download, model and analyze street networks and other OSM features as NetworkX graphs.
why_it_matters: Rapid road/path graph construction for planners and task allocation experiments in Python.
hackathon_notes: pip install osmnx; needs internet for Overpass unless you load a local OSM file.

name: elevation
summary: CLI/Python tool to download, cache and clip global DEMs (SRTM, Copernicus DEM and others) for a bounding box.
why_it_matters: One-command DEM for an AOI, the first input for terrain-referenced navigation and terrain-aware planning.
hackathon_notes: Needs GDAL on PATH; eio clip --bounds ... produces a GeoTIFF.

name: TileServer GL
summary: Vector and raster tile server that serves MBTiles/PMTiles with GL styles and renders raster tiles server-side with MapLibre Native.
why_it_matters: Simplest offline basemap server for field laptops and TAK clients needing raster tiles.
hackathon_notes: docker run maptiler/tileserver-gl with an mbtiles file; also gives WMTS for QGIS.

name: Martin
summary: Fast Rust tile server for PostGIS, MBTiles and PMTiles sources, with tile generation and mbtiles tooling.
why_it_matters: Serves live PostGIS layers (tracks, zones) as vector tiles alongside static basemaps.
hackathon_notes: Single binary or docker; point at a PostGIS table to stream dynamic features.

name: PMTiles
summary: Single-file tile archive format and tooling, served by HTTP range requests from static storage, with JS/Go readers and extraction CLI.
why_it_matters: Ship an entire regional basemap as one file on a USB stick or static server - ideal for disconnected ops.
hackathon_notes: pmtiles extract from a planet build to cut your AOI; load with the MapLibre protocol plugin.

name: Planetiler
summary: Fast vector tile generator that builds OpenMapTiles-compatible tilesets from OSM extracts on a single machine.
why_it_matters: Build your own up-to-date offline basemap for an AOI in minutes.
hackathon_notes: java -jar planetiler.jar --area=<region> outputs mbtiles or pmtiles.

name: mgrs (Python)
summary: Python library converting between latitude/longitude and MGRS grid references, built on NGA GEOTRANS 3.10 (now a Rust port exposed through a pybind11 extension).
why_it_matters: MGRS is the grid language of military users; needed for any C2 UI or report generator.
hackathon_notes: pip install mgrs; mind the precision argument for 1 m vs 10 m references. Since 1.6.0 inverse conversion returns the grid-cell centre, not the south-west corner.

name: GeographicLib
summary: C++ library for accurate geodesic problems, UTM/UPS/MGRS conversions, geoid heights, gravity and magnetic field models.
why_it_matters: Gold-standard geodesy: geodesic distances, geoid (EGM96/2008) undulation for GNSS height vs DEM height, and MGRS.
hackathon_notes: Python and JS ports exist (geographiclib-python, geographiclib-js); geoid datasets download separately.

name: pymap3d
summary: Pure-Python 3D coordinate conversions: geodetic, ECEF, ENU, NED, AER, ECI, with optional NumPy vectorization.
why_it_matters: The everyday tool for converting GNSS fixes into a local ENU/NED frame for fusion and planning.
hackathon_notes: pip install pymap3d; no compiled deps.

name: sentinelhub-py
summary: Python client for Sentinel Hub and Copernicus Data Space services to search, download and process Sentinel and other satellite imagery.
why_it_matters: Pull recent satellite imagery of an AOI to build reference maps for visual geolocalization.
hackathon_notes: Needs free Copernicus Data Space or Sentinel Hub credentials; set up before the event.

name: pystac-client
summary: Python client for searching STAC APIs (Earth Search, Planetary Computer and others) by area, time and properties.
why_it_matters: Credential-free path to Sentinel-2, Landsat and Copernicus DEM tiles via public STAC catalogs.
hackathon_notes: Search Earth Search (AWS) without a key and read COGs directly with rasterio.

name: odc-stac
summary: Loads STAC items into xarray datasets with reprojection, resampling and mosaicking.
why_it_matters: Turn a STAC search into a ready, aligned raster stack for map-matching experiments.
hackathon_notes: Works with Dask for larger AOIs.

name: OpenDroneMap (ODM)
summary: Photogrammetry toolkit that turns aerial images into orthophotos, point clouds, 3D models and DEMs.
why_it_matters: Build your own up-to-date reference orthophoto and DSM from a survey flight for visual and terrain navigation.
hackathon_notes: docker run opendronemap/odm on a folder of images; WebODM gives a GUI. Processing time scales with image count.

name: TAK Server (open source)
summary: Open-source release of the TAK Server from the TAK Product Center: the federation and message routing server for ATAK/WinTAK/iTAK clients, handling CoT, data packages, missions and video.
why_it_matters: Reference C2 backend used by many government users; integrating with it makes a demo interoperable with fielded TAK clients.
hackathon_notes: Java + PostgreSQL + certificate setup is the main hurdle; use a docker recipe and allow several hours.

name: GoATAK
summary: Go implementation of a simple ATAK-compatible server and a web client, supporting CoT over TCP/UDP/SSL.
why_it_matters: Single static binary TAK server and browser client - minimal footprint for edge devices.
hackathon_notes: go build or release binary; web map client is handy for judges without ATAK installed.

name: CloudTAK
summary: Browser-based TAK-compatible common operating picture with ETL connectors that push external data feeds into TAK.
why_it_matters: Shows how to bridge arbitrary data sources (sensors, APIs) into a TAK network with a web COP.
hackathon_notes: AWS-oriented deployment; locally, reuse its node-CoT library and connector patterns.

name: node-CoT
summary: JavaScript/TypeScript library for parsing, building and converting Cursor-on-Target messages, including GeoJSON conversion and TAK protobuf.
why_it_matters: Quickest way to emit CoT from a Node/web app.
hackathon_notes: npm install @tak-ps/node-cot.

name: takproto
summary: Encode and decode TAK protobuf (TAK Protocol v1) packets, including mesh and stream formats.
why_it_matters: Needed when talking to modern TAK clients that prefer protobuf over XML CoT.
hackathon_notes: pip install takproto.

name: cotlib (Go)
summary: Go library for parsing, validating and generating Cursor-on-Target XML with security-focused input limits and optional schema validation.
why_it_matters: Hardened CoT parsing for Go services that accept untrusted network input.
hackathon_notes: Schema validation needs libxml2 and CGO.

name: milsymbol
summary: Pure JavaScript library generating MIL-STD-2525 (B/C/D/E) and APP-6 (B/D/E) military symbols as SVG or canvas.
why_it_matters: Renders correct unit and track symbology on any web map without licensed assets.
hackathon_notes: npm install milsymbol; new ms.Symbol(sidc).asSVG() drops straight into a Leaflet or MapLibre marker.

name: Joint Military Symbology XML
summary: Esri data encapsulation of MIL-STD-2525D and APP-6(D) symbology: symbol IDs, entity tables and SVG assets.
why_it_matters: Machine-readable symbol tables useful for validating SIDCs or building your own renderer.
hackathon_notes: Archived in 2024; data still useful.

name: ASTERIX decoder (Croatia Control)
summary: C/C++ and Python decoder for EUROCONTROL ASTERIX surveillance data from files, stdin or network, with XML category definitions and JSON/XML output.
why_it_matters: ASTERIX is the format real radars and ATC surveillance use; decoding it lets a demo ingest professional air picture feeds.
hackathon_notes: Python module is on PyPI as asterix_decoder; feed it recorded or live UDP ASTERIX and get JSON per record.

name: asterix-specs
summary: EUROCONTROL ASTERIX category specifications in a structured machine-readable format, with generated JSON and docs.
why_it_matters: Authoritative-structured spec source for building ASTERIX encoders/decoders in any language.
hackathon_notes: Companion asterix-libs repo has generated Python libraries.

name: pyModeS
summary: Python decoder for Mode S and ADS-B messages including Comm-B / EHS fields, with live streaming tools.
why_it_matters: Decode raw Mode S yourself, including derived wind and airspeed data; underlies The 1090MHz Riddle book.
hackathon_notes: pip install pyModeS; pairs with a Beast/raw feed from readsb.

name: traffic
summary: Toolbox for processing and analyzing air traffic trajectories: OpenSky access, filtering, resampling, airspace intersection and visualization.
why_it_matters: Analyze flight tracks and airspace structures for airspace awareness or UAV deconfliction studies.
hackathon_notes: pip install traffic; OpenSky historical data needs an account.

name: OpenSky API clients
summary: Python and Java bindings for the OpenSky Network REST API for live and recent aircraft states.
why_it_matters: Free crowd-sourced air picture when no local receiver is available.
hackathon_notes: Anonymous access is rate-limited. Since March 2026 authenticated access uses OAuth2 client credentials (basic auth was dropped); create an API client in your OpenSky account.

name: Gazebo Sim (gz-sim)
summary: Current-generation Gazebo robotics simulator with pluggable physics, rendering and a large sensor library (IMU, GPS/NavSat, lidar, cameras, magnetometer, altimeter). Successor to Gazebo Classic.
why_it_matters: The default SITL backend for both PX4 and ArduPilot today; the place to inject sensor noise, GNSS dropouts and degraded conditions into a full autopilot stack.
hackathon_notes: Install a binary release (Harmonic or later) plus ros_gz. Pair with PX4 'make px4_sitl gz_x500' or ardupilot_gazebo. GPU helps for camera sensors; headless server mode works for CI.

name: ros_gz bridge
summary: Bridge packages that relay topics, services and clock between Gazebo Sim transport and ROS 1/ROS 2.
why_it_matters: Needed whenever a ROS 2 navigation or SLAM stack has to consume simulated sensor streams from Gazebo.
hackathon_notes: Use parameter_bridge with a YAML of topic mappings. Match the ros_gz branch to your ROS 2 distro and Gazebo release or builds fail.

name: PX4 Gazebo models
summary: Model and world repository for the new Gazebo, used by PX4 SITL targets such as gz_x500.
why_it_matters: Shows how PX4 vehicles and sensors are described for gz-sim; the starting point for adding custom sensors to a PX4 airframe.
hackathon_notes: Fetched automatically by PX4 SITL. Fork and edit SDF to add cameras or change sensor noise.

name: jMAVSim
summary: Lightweight Java multirotor simulator that speaks MAVLink to PX4, without a 3D-world physics engine.
why_it_matters: Fastest way to get a PX4 SITL quad flying for MAVLink, GCS or mission-logic work when sensors and worlds do not matter.
hackathon_notes: Runs with 'make px4_sitl jmavsim'. Needs a JDK. No cameras or lidar, so not for perception work.

name: ArduPilot SITL Models
summary: Collection of aircraft and vehicle models and parameter files for ArduPilot SITL across several simulator backends.
why_it_matters: Ready-made airframes (including fixed-wing and VTOL) save hours when a hackathon scenario needs something other than a quadcopter.
hackathon_notes: Pick a model folder and follow its readme; each lists the backend it targets.

name: AirSim
summary: Unreal Engine based simulator for drones and cars with camera, depth, lidar, IMU, GPS, barometer and magnetometer models and a Python/C++ API. Microsoft wound down development and pointed users to Project AirSim.
why_it_matters: Still the most widely used photorealistic drone sim in research papers; many visual-nav and geolocalization datasets were rendered with it.
hackathon_notes: Prebuilt binary environments are the quickest path. Building from source requires a matching old Unreal version. For new work prefer Colosseum or Project AirSim.

name: Colosseum (AirSim fork)
summary: Community fork of AirSim that moved it to newer Unreal Engine 5 releases. The GitHub repository is now marked archived.
why_it_matters: Was the main path to run AirSim on UE5; useful as a reference port even though it is no longer maintained.
hackathon_notes: Archived on GitHub, so expect unanswered issues. Use only if you need its UE5 changes specifically.

name: Project AirSim
summary: Open-source release of Project AirSim, the rewrite and successor of AirSim, for building and testing autonomous aerial systems in high-fidelity Unreal environments.
why_it_matters: The actively developed line of the AirSim family, relevant for photorealistic aerial perception and autonomy testing.
hackathon_notes: Check its docs for supported Unreal version and OS. Heavier setup than AirSim binaries; budget several hours.

name: FlightGoggles
summary: Unity3D and ROS framework from MIT for photorealistic camera rendering with real or simulated vehicle dynamics in the loop.
why_it_matters: Pioneered vehicle-in-the-loop rendering: fly a real drone in a mocap room while feeding it synthetic imagery.
hackathon_notes: Not actively maintained since 2024; ROS1. Mostly of interest as a reference or alongside the Blackbird dataset.

name: Pegasus Simulator
summary: Framework on top of NVIDIA Isaac Sim for simulating multirotors with PX4 in the loop and Python-defined vehicles and sensors.
why_it_matters: Gives PX4 users photorealistic, GPU-accelerated Omniverse rendering while keeping the real autopilot stack.
hackathon_notes: Needs an RTX GPU and an Isaac Sim install; match Pegasus release to the Isaac Sim version listed in its docs.

name: NVIDIA Isaac Sim
summary: NVIDIA's Omniverse-based robot simulator, now open source, with RTX sensor simulation (cameras, lidar, IMU) and ROS 2 bridges.
why_it_matters: Base layer for Pegasus, OmniDrones and Isaac Lab; strong for synthetic data generation for perception models.
hackathon_notes: RTX GPU and a lot of disk required. Use the prebuilt container or pip install rather than building from source in a hackathon.

name: Isaac Lab
summary: Robot-learning framework on Isaac Sim for massively parallel RL and imitation learning, with navigation and locomotion task examples.
why_it_matters: Fast route to training learned navigation or locomotion policies with thousands of parallel simulated robots.
hackathon_notes: Install via pip on a supported Isaac Sim version. Start from an existing nav task config rather than writing environments from scratch.

name: CARLA
summary: Open-source autonomous-driving simulator on Unreal with camera, lidar, radar, GNSS and IMU sensors, traffic and weather control.
why_it_matters: Standard ground-vehicle testbed for localization and planning under weather, night and sensor-degradation conditions.
hackathon_notes: Use packaged releases and the Python client; the ROS 2 bridge is separate. A decent GPU is required.

name: RotorS
summary: Gazebo Classic MAV simulator from ETH ASL with multirotor models, IMU and odometry sensor plugins and example controllers.
why_it_matters: Classic reference for MAV sim used in many VIO and planning papers; its IMU noise models are still frequently copied.
hackathon_notes: ROS1 and Gazebo Classic only; use for reproducing older papers rather than new builds.

name: Aerial Gym Simulator
summary: GPU-parallel aerial-robot simulator from NTNU ARL built on NVIDIA Isaac Gym, with depth/range sensors and RL navigation examples.
why_it_matters: Train learned obstacle avoidance and navigation for drones at scale with simulated depth cameras and lidar.
hackathon_notes: Needs NVIDIA GPU and Isaac Gym preview (a legacy package); check README for current install path.

name: gym-pybullet-drones
summary: Gymnasium environments on PyBullet for single and multi-agent quadcopter control and RL (formerly under utiasDSL).
why_it_matters: Lowest-friction multi-drone RL sandbox: pure Python, CPU-only, quick to modify.
hackathon_notes: pip install in a venv and run examples within minutes. No photorealistic sensors; good for control, swarming and planning logic.

name: OmniDrones
summary: GPU-parallel drone simulation and RL platform built on Isaac Sim.
why_it_matters: Supports multi-drone and transport tasks with vectorized environments for learning-based autonomy.
hackathon_notes: Pinned to specific Isaac Sim versions; check compatibility before investing time.

name: RotorPy
summary: Python multirotor simulator with aerodynamic effects (drag, wind) for education and research.
why_it_matters: Good for studying estimator and controller behaviour under wind and disturbances without a game engine.
hackathon_notes: pip installable, runs on a laptop. Has IMU and mocap-style sensor models; add your own estimator in Python.

name: Webots
summary: General-purpose open-source robot simulator with many robot models and sensors including GPS, compass, IMU, lidar and radar.
why_it_matters: Cross-platform and easy to install; good for ground and multi-robot nav demos with ROS 2 integration.
hackathon_notes: Installers for Windows, macOS and Linux. webots_ros2 package for ROS 2. Less common in aerial autonomy.

name: HoloOcean (documentation)
summary: Documentation repository for HoloOcean, BYU's Unreal-based underwater simulator with sonar, DVL, IMU, depth and camera sensors and multi-agent support. The simulator code itself is not hosted in this repo.
why_it_matters: Photorealistic underwater sim aimed at marine navigation and SLAM research, including acoustic modems for multi-agent setups.
hackathon_notes: Follow the installation page of the docs; Python package plus downloadable worlds. Heavy GPU load for sonar rendering.

name: GRID playground (AirGen)
summary: Notebooks and examples for the GRID platform from Scaled Foundations, which pairs the AirSim-derived AirGen simulator with foundation-model perception and LLM-driven robot control.
why_it_matters: Shows a sim plus foundation-model workflow for aerial autonomy, close to 'LLM in the loop' hackathon ideas.
hackathon_notes: Uses the hosted GRID platform for the sim side; check account requirements before relying on it.

name: JSBSim
summary: Open-source flight dynamics model library for fixed-wing and other aircraft, used by FlightGear and as an ArduPilot SITL backend.
why_it_matters: Credible fixed-wing dynamics for testing navigation filters on aircraft profiles rather than quadcopters.
hackathon_notes: Python bindings via pip. Combine with ArduPilot SITL for an autopilot loop.

name: MARSIM
summary: Lightweight point-realistic lidar simulator for UAVs from HKU MaRS, supporting rotating and solid-state lidar patterns.
why_it_matters: Fast way to test lidar-based UAV navigation and planning without a full game-engine sim.
hackathon_notes: ROS based; runs on CPU or modest GPU. Pairs well with FAST-LIO-style stacks.

name: ESIM
summary: Event camera simulator from UZH RPG that renders event streams from simulated scenes.
why_it_matters: Generates event-camera data for high-speed or low-light VIO research without hardware.
hackathon_notes: ROS1 and older build tooling. For converting existing video to events, rpg_vid2e is easier.

name: evo
summary: Python package and CLI for evaluating odometry and SLAM trajectories (ATE/RPE, alignment, plotting) in TUM, KITTI, EuRoC and ROS bag formats.
why_it_matters: The default way to score a nav or SLAM result against ground truth; essential for any demo that claims accuracy.
hackathon_notes: pip install evo. Run evo_ape with alignment flags; it reads most dataset ground-truth formats directly.

name: rpg_trajectory_evaluation
summary: Toolbox for quantitative trajectory evaluation of VO/VIO, implementing the alignment and relative-error protocol from Zhang & Scaramuzza (IROS 2018).
why_it_matters: Implements the alignment conventions used in many VIO benchmarks; good for apples-to-apples comparisons.
hackathon_notes: Old Python 2 era code, ROS optional. evo is easier for quick use.

name: pykitti
summary: Python loaders for the KITTI raw and odometry datasets.
why_it_matters: Removes boilerplate when using KITTI's GPS/IMU, lidar and stereo data for localization experiments.
hackathon_notes: pip install pykitti and point it at the dataset folders.

name: UZH-FPV dataset tools
summary: Companion repo for the UZH-FPV drone racing dataset with scripts and info.
why_it_matters: Aggressive high-speed drone sequences stress VIO well beyond EuRoC.
hackathon_notes: Inactive since 2020; dataset itself is on the UZH site.

name: Hilti SLAM Challenge 2022
summary: Repository for the 2022 Hilti SLAM Challenge with dataset info and evaluation tooling.
why_it_matters: Construction-site sequences with accurate ground truth; a strong test of lidar/visual-inertial SLAM in GNSS-denied indoor spaces.
hackathon_notes: Download bags from the challenge site; scoring scripts in repo.

name: Hilti SLAM Challenge 2023
summary: Repository for the 2023 Hilti SLAM Challenge, including multi-session sequences.
why_it_matters: Multi-session data is useful for map reuse and relocalization experiments.
hackathon_notes: Same workflow as 2022; check the challenge site for current download links.

name: MCD: Multi-Campus Dataset
summary: Site repo for MCD, a multi-campus dataset across Asia and Europe with spinning and non-repetitive lidar, stereo cameras, IMUs, UWB ranging, survey-grade prior maps and continuous-time ground truth.
why_it_matters: Covers localization against prior maps and UWB-aided fusion in large outdoor areas.
hackathon_notes: Data downloads and tutorials are linked from the site.

name: NTU VIRAL dataset
summary: Site repo for NTU VIRAL, an aerial dataset with lidars, cameras, IMU and UWB ranging from a drone.
why_it_matters: Rare UWB-equipped drone dataset for range-aided fusion experiments.
hackathon_notes: ROS bags; download links on the site.

name: M2DGR
summary: Multi-modal, multi-scenario ground robot dataset from SJTU with cameras, lidar, IMU, GNSS and more, indoor and outdoor.
why_it_matters: Indoor/outdoor transitions with GNSS make it useful for testing GNSS-loss handling in fusion.
hackathon_notes: ROS bags; check repo for download mirrors.

name: GVINS dataset
summary: Dataset with synchronized visual, inertial and raw GNSS measurements released with GVINS.
why_it_matters: One of few datasets with raw GNSS pseudoranges plus camera and IMU, needed for tightly coupled GNSS-VIO.
hackathon_notes: ROS bags with custom GNSS message types; install the gnss_comm package.

name: UrbanNav
summary: Open multisensor urban positioning dataset from PolyU IPNL with GNSS, IMU, lidar and camera in deep urban canyons.
why_it_matters: Benchmark for GNSS multipath and NLOS mitigation in cities.
hackathon_notes: Pick one Hong Kong sequence and run an RTKLIB plus loosely coupled baseline to show urban degradation.

name: ALTO
summary: Aerial-view, large-scale, terrain-oriented dataset for aerial place recognition and localization.
why_it_matters: Directly targets UAV localization over terrain when GNSS is unavailable.
hackathon_notes: Inactive since 2022; check that the download links still work before planning around it.

name: VPAIR
summary: Repo for VPAIR, an aerial visual place recognition dataset matching low-altitude flight imagery to reference orthophotos.
why_it_matters: Benchmark for UAV visual geolocalization against georeferenced maps.
hackathon_notes: Small enough to evaluate quickly with VPR-methods-evaluation.

name: AerialVL
summary: Visual geo-localization dataset and code designed for aerial vehicles.
why_it_matters: Another aerial-to-map benchmark with sequential flights, useful for testing filtering over VPR outputs.
hackathon_notes: Check README for map tile download steps.

name: Mapillary SLS
summary: Tools for the Mapillary Street-level Sequences dataset for lifelong visual place recognition.
why_it_matters: Large, diverse street-level VPR benchmark used to train many current VPR models.
hackathon_notes: Dataset download needs registration on Mapillary.

name: VPR-Bench
summary: Open-source visual place recognition evaluation framework from the IJCV paper, with many datasets and techniques integrated.
why_it_matters: Ready harness to compare VPR methods across conditions and viewpoints.
hackathon_notes: Older dependencies; consider VPR-methods-evaluation for modern models.

name: tartanairpy
summary: Python package for downloading, customizing and iterating the TartanAir-V2 synthetic dataset.
why_it_matters: TartanAir's photorealistic scenes with weather and lighting variety stress-test SLAM and VO.
hackathon_notes: Download only the environments and modalities you need - full set is very large.

name: pyboreas
summary: Devkit for the Boreas multi-season driving dataset with radar, lidar, camera and GNSS/INS ground truth.
why_it_matters: Radar plus lidar over seasons and snow suits all-weather localization work.
hackathon_notes: Data is hosted on S3; download selected sequences.

name: Oxford RobotCar SDK
summary: SDK for the Oxford RobotCar dataset with loaders and projection tools.
why_it_matters: Long-term, all-condition driving data is a staple for localization and place recognition research.
hackathon_notes: Inactive since 2022; Python and MATLAB helpers still work.

name: Blackbird dataset
summary: MIT dataset of aggressive indoor quadrotor flights with real IMU and motor data and rendered camera imagery.
why_it_matters: Combines real flight dynamics with synthetic vision, good for VIO under aggressive motion.
hackathon_notes: Inactive since 2022; download scripts may need adaptation.

name: ORB-SLAM2
summary: Feature-based SLAM for monocular, stereo and RGB-D cameras using ORB features, with loop closing and relocalization against a reusable map.
why_it_matters: The reference visual SLAM baseline most papers compare against; cheap camera-only localization when GNSS is denied.
hackathon_notes: Superseded by ORB-SLAM3 and no longer developed; builds need patching on modern OpenCV/Eigen. Use only to reproduce old baselines.

name: ORB-SLAM3
summary: Visual, visual-inertial and multi-map SLAM supporting monocular, stereo and RGB-D cameras with pinhole and fisheye models, using a map atlas to survive tracking loss.
why_it_matters: Still the most cited open VI-SLAM system; a solid GNSS-denied drift baseline for drones and ground robots.
hackathon_notes: Build against Pangolin, OpenCV and Eigen; expect a few compile fixes. Run on EuRoC or TUM-VI first, then your own camera after Kalibr calibration. Upstream sees little activity.

name: ORB_SLAM3_ROS2
summary: ROS 2 wrapper package that exposes ORB-SLAM3 as nodes for monocular, stereo and RGB-D input.
why_it_matters: Shortest path to running ORB-SLAM3 inside a ROS 2 robot stack.
hackathon_notes: Needs a working ORB-SLAM3 build first; check the README for the ROS 2 distro it targets before choosing your Docker base image.

name: VINS-Mono
summary: Optimization-based monocular visual-inertial estimator with sliding-window bundle adjustment, online initialization, loop closure and pose-graph reuse.
why_it_matters: The canonical one-camera-plus-IMU estimator; works on light UAV payloads where stereo or LiDAR is too heavy.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1 only and no longer maintained; run in a Melodic/Noetic container. Sensitive to time sync and initialization motion.

name: VINS-Fusion
summary: Extension of VINS-Mono supporting mono+IMU, stereo, and stereo+IMU, with optional loose fusion of global sensors such as GPS.
why_it_matters: Shows how to plug intermittent GNSS into a VIO estimator, which is the core pattern for degraded-PNT navigation.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1; use a Docker image. The global-fusion node is a good template for injecting GNSS when it is trusted and dropping it when jammed.

name: OpenVINS
summary: MSCKF-based visual-inertial navigation platform with online calibration, a simulator, and extensive documentation for research use.
why_it_matters: Probably the best-documented VIO codebase; filter-based, light enough for embedded boards.
hackathon_notes: Supports ROS 1 and ROS 2. Its built-in simulator lets you test without hardware on day one. Docs site explains every estimator component.

name: MINS
summary: Multi-sensor aided inertial navigation that fuses IMU with camera, LiDAR, GNSS and wheel odometry, including online spatial/temporal calibration and a multi-sensor simulator.
why_it_matters: Directly relevant to assured PNT: one estimator that degrades gracefully as individual sensors (including GNSS) drop out.
hackathon_notes: Start with the provided simulated data to see each sensor's contribution, then disable GNSS mid-run to demo a jamming scenario.

name: Kimera-VIO
summary: Stereo visual-inertial odometry with a factor-graph backend, robust loop closure and real-time 3D mesh generation; the odometry core of the Kimera stack.
why_it_matters: Gives both a pose and a lightweight 3D mesh, useful for situational-awareness displays.
hackathon_notes: Heavier build (GTSAM, OpenGV, DBoW2); use the Docker setup. The ROS wrapper lives in a separate repo.

name: Kimera-RPGO
summary: Robust pose-graph optimization that rejects bad loop closures via pairwise consistency maximization on top of GTSAM.
why_it_matters: Outlier-robust loop closure is what keeps a long GNSS-denied mission from corrupting its map; reusable outside Kimera.
hackathon_notes: Small library; feed it any odometry + loop closure edges. Good drop-in back end for a custom front end.

name: Basalt
summary: GitHub mirror of Basalt, a visual-inertial odometry and mapping system built around non-linear factor recovery, with calibration tools; primary development is on GitLab.
why_it_matters: Fast, accurate stereo VIO that runs well on CPUs; also ships camera-IMU calibration.
hackathon_notes: Submit issues upstream on GitLab. Builds cleanly on Ubuntu; ROS integration is via community wrappers.

name: SVO Pro
summary: Open release of SVO Pro: semi-direct visual(-inertial) odometry with fisheye/omni camera support, optional global map and loop closure.
why_it_matters: Very low-latency front end suited to fast agile flight on compute-limited drones.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1 / catkin build; dormant since 2024. Good when CPU budget is tight.

name: DSO (Direct Sparse Odometry)
summary: Direct monocular visual odometry that optimizes photometric error over a sparse set of pixels with joint photometric calibration.
why_it_matters: Works in low-texture scenes where feature-based methods fail; the basis for DM-VIO and many direct methods.
hackathon_notes: No IMU, no loop closure, scale-ambiguous; mostly useful as a building block or comparison.

name: DM-VIO
summary: Monocular visual-inertial odometry built on DSO using delayed marginalization and pose-graph bundle adjustment for IMU initialization.
why_it_matters: Strong monocular VIO accuracy; good for single-camera drones.
hackathon_notes: Standalone build with an optional ROS wrapper repo. Expects photometrically calibrated input for best results.

name: ROVIO
summary: Robust visual-inertial odometry using an iterated EKF directly on image-patch photometric errors.
why_it_matters: Long a go-to VIO on PX4/MAV research platforms because it is cheap to run.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1 / catkin. Lightweight; tuning of patch and feature counts matters.

name: MSCKF_VIO
summary: Stereo multi-state constraint Kalman filter VIO designed for fast autonomous flight.
why_it_matters: Lean filter-based stereo VIO that runs comfortably on embedded CPUs.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1; unmaintained. Tested heavily on EuRoC; good comparison point to OpenVINS.

name: OKVIS2
summary: Keyframe-based visual-inertial SLAM with loop closure and a realtime scalable factor-graph design; second generation of OKVIS.
why_it_matters: Mature research VI-SLAM from the ETH/TUM lineage with active maintenance.
hackathon_notes: CMake build; check the README for ROS integration and the camera/IMU config format for your sensor.

name: OKVIS2-X
summary: Extension of OKVIS2 that can additionally use dense depth or LiDAR and fuse GNSS.
why_it_matters: Recent (2025-2026) multi-sensor VI-SLAM that includes GNSS fusion, matching assured-PNT architectures.
hackathon_notes: New codebase; expect some setup friction. Good showcase for switching GNSS on/off.

name: AirSLAM
summary: Point-and-line visual(-inertial) SLAM using learned features, designed for illumination-robust operation, with TensorRT acceleration; successor to AirVO.
why_it_matters: Targets lighting changes (dawn/dusk/night), a common failure mode for camera navigation.
hackathon_notes: Needs an NVIDIA GPU (TensorRT). Docker recommended.

name: maplab
summary: Modular multi-session, multi-modal mapping framework with map merging, optimization and localization against saved maps.
why_it_matters: Build a map once, then localize repeatedly against it; supports multi-robot and multi-session merges.
hackathon_notes: Large ROS 1 codebase; only worth it if you need persistent map management.

name: RTAB-Map
summary: Graph-based SLAM library and app supporting RGB-D, stereo and LiDAR, with memory management for large-scale loop closure and map reuse.
why_it_matters: Practical all-rounder with GUI, database and localization modes; easiest way to get a working 3D map on a ground robot.
hackathon_notes: Install via apt binaries (ROS) or the standalone app. Supports phone/iPad LiDAR capture. Save a map, then switch to localization mode.

name: rtabmap_ros
summary: ROS and ROS 2 integration for RTAB-Map, exposing SLAM, localization and odometry nodes.
why_it_matters: Drop-in SLAM for ROS 2 Nav2 stacks.
hackathon_notes: apt-installable for supported distros; launch examples cover common sensors.

name: DROID-SLAM
summary: Deep visual SLAM that iterates dense bundle adjustment through a recurrent update operator, for monocular, stereo and RGB-D input.
why_it_matters: Much more robust than classic pipelines on hard sequences; strong learned baseline.
hackathon_notes: Needs a large-memory NVIDIA GPU; not real-time on embedded. Pretrained weights available.

name: DPVO / DPV-SLAM
summary: Deep Patch Visual Odometry: learned sparse patch tracking for VO, plus DPV-SLAM with loop closure.
why_it_matters: Lighter learned VO than DROID-SLAM, closer to real-time on a desktop GPU.
hackathon_notes: CUDA build of custom kernels; follow the conda instructions.

name: MASt3R-SLAM
summary: Real-time dense monocular SLAM built on the MASt3R two-view 3D reconstruction prior, needing no fixed camera model (CVPR 2025).
why_it_matters: Works with uncalibrated cameras, useful for opportunistic imagery from unknown cameras.
hackathon_notes: Requires a capable NVIDIA GPU and model checkpoint downloads. Great demo value on handheld video.

name: VGGT
summary: Visual Geometry Grounded Transformer: a feed-forward network predicting camera poses, depth and point maps from one or many images (CVPR 2025 best paper).
why_it_matters: Instant pose and geometry from a handful of frames; a building block for learned relocalization and mapping.
hackathon_notes: GPU inference via PyTorch; Hugging Face demo for quick tests. Not a full SLAM system by itself.

name: MonoGS (Gaussian Splatting SLAM)
summary: Gaussian-splatting SLAM for monocular, stereo and RGB-D cameras that tracks and maps directly against a 3D Gaussian representation.
why_it_matters: Produces photorealistic maps useful for operator situational awareness and later simulation.
hackathon_notes: Needs a strong GPU; not real-time on embedded hardware. Best as an offline mapping demo.

name: SplaTAM
summary: Dense RGB-D SLAM that tracks and maps using 3D Gaussians and differentiable rendering (CVPR 2024).
why_it_matters: Reference Gaussian-splatting SLAM for RGB-D sensors.
hackathon_notes: GPU-heavy and slower than real time; good for offline indoor captures.

name: Photo-SLAM
summary: Couples ORB-SLAM3-style geometric tracking with a photorealistic Gaussian map for monocular, stereo and RGB-D cameras (CVPR 2024).
why_it_matters: Classic robust tracking plus a nice-looking map, closer to real time than pure splatting SLAM.
hackathon_notes: LibTorch + CUDA build; check version pins carefully.

name: ESVO
summary: Event-based stereo visual odometry using spatio-temporal consistency of two event cameras for mapping and tracking.
why_it_matters: Event cameras keep working under high dynamic range and fast motion, where frame cameras blur or saturate.
hackathon_notes: Needs stereo event cameras or recorded datasets; ROS 1.

name: Ultimate SLAM
summary: Open-source release of Ultimate SLAM, combining events, standard frames and IMU for VIO in HDR and high-speed scenarios (RA-L 2018).
why_it_matters: Template for fusing event cameras with frames and IMU for robust flight state estimation.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1 / catkin; test on event datasets before buying hardware.

name: Event-based Vision Resources
summary: Community-curated list of event-camera papers, datasets, drivers, simulators and code.
why_it_matters: Fastest way to find event-camera datasets and odometry code.
hackathon_notes: Use as a discovery index; not runnable code.

name: HKU Event-based VO/VIO/SLAM
summary: Dataset and index of event-based VO, VIO and SLAM work from HKU ArcLab, including stereo event sequences.
why_it_matters: Ready-made event data for testing event odometry without hardware.
hackathon_notes: Download sequences as rosbags; pair with ESVO.

name: ROVTIO
summary: Visual-thermal-inertial odometry extending ROVIO to fuse asynchronous thermal and visual images with IMU, switching to whichever camera is informative.
why_it_matters: Thermal keeps odometry alive in darkness and smoke; NTNU ARL targets subterranean and degraded environments.
hackathon_notes: Needs a thermal camera synced to IMU (or their datasets). Thermal calibration targets need a heated pattern.

name: ETIO
summary: Edge-based monocular thermal-inertial odometry that tracks thermal edges for visually degraded environments.
why_it_matters: Low-cost night/smoke navigation from a single thermal camera plus IMU.
hackathon_notes: Code released with the paper; try on public thermal datasets first.

name: RRxIO
summary: Radar visual/thermal inertial odometry fusing 4D mmWave radar with a visual or thermal camera and IMU for degraded visual conditions.
why_it_matters: Radar plus thermal is a strong combination for fog, smoke and darkness.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1; datasets released by the author. Good for a degraded-visibility demo.

name: RIO
summary: EKF-based radar-inertial odometry using 4D mmWave radar ego-velocity measurements.
why_it_matters: Cheap automotive radars give velocity in fog/smoke/darkness; a minimal radar odometry template.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1; uses the author's radar ego-velocity estimator. Works with TI mmWave-class sensors.

name: 4DRadarSLAM
summary: 4D radar SLAM with scan-to-scan registration, loop closure and pose-graph optimization, released with an NTU 4D radar dataset.
why_it_matters: One of the few full SLAM pipelines for 4D imaging radar, the all-weather sensor for ground vehicles.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1; structured like hdl_graph_slam. Test on their dataset first.

name: CFEAR Radarodometry
summary: Learning-free spinning-radar odometry that filters returns to sparse oriented surface points and registers against keyframes.
why_it_matters: Strong baseline for spinning (Navtech-style) radar odometry; robust in weather that defeats LiDAR.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1; benchmarked on Oxford Radar RobotCar and Boreas.

name: Go-RIO
summary: Ground-optimized 4D radar-inertial odometry integrating continuous velocity via Gaussian processes (ICRA 2025 best paper finalist).
why_it_matters: Recent state of the art for 4D radar odometry on ground vehicles.
hackathon_notes: Recent code; check sensor assumptions against your radar.

name: Gaussian-RIO
summary: 4D radar-inertial odometry using Gaussian modeling of radar points and multi-hypothesis scan matching.
why_it_matters: Another recent open 4D radar odometry baseline, useful for comparison.
hackathon_notes: Small research codebase; read the paper before integrating.

name: LIO-SAM
summary: Tightly coupled LiDAR-inertial odometry via factor-graph smoothing, with optional GPS factors and loop closure.
why_it_matters: Popular LIO with built-in GNSS factors; the template for LiDAR+INS+intermittent GNSS.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1 main branch, community ROS 2 branch. Needs a 9-axis IMU and careful extrinsics.

name: FAST-LIO / FAST-LIO2
summary: Computationally efficient LiDAR-inertial odometry using an iterated error-state Kalman filter and incremental k-d tree map, mapping raw points directly.
why_it_matters: The default LIO in many field robots; runs on ARM boards and supports solid-state and spinning LiDARs.
hackathon_notes: Easiest LIO to get running; Livox drivers supported. No loop closure; pair with a localization or loop-closure add-on.

name: Point-LIO
summary: High-bandwidth LiDAR-inertial odometry that updates the state point by point, tolerating aggressive motion and IMU saturation.
why_it_matters: Handles violent motion (agile drones, vibration) where frame-based LIO breaks.
hackathon_notes: Same ecosystem as FAST-LIO; try when FAST-LIO diverges on aggressive motion.

name: FAST-LIVO2
summary: Direct LiDAR-inertial-visual odometry fusing LiDAR, camera and IMU in a sequential ESIKF update with a unified voxel map.
why_it_matters: High-accuracy colored mapping that stays robust when either LiDAR or camera degrades.
hackathon_notes: Needs hardware-synced LiDAR+camera; datasets available.

name: R3LIVE
summary: Tightly coupled LiDAR-inertial-visual estimation and RGB-colored mapping package.
why_it_matters: Produces dense colored maps useful for operator displays and mapping.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1, heavy on dependencies; FAST-LIVO2 is the newer alternative.

name: KISS-ICP
summary: Minimal LiDAR odometry based on point-to-point ICP with adaptive thresholding, working across sensors with few parameters.
why_it_matters: Works out of the box on almost any LiDAR without IMU; ideal hackathon starting point.
hackathon_notes: `pip install kiss-icp` and run on a rosbag or KITTI folder in minutes. Add KISS-SLAM for loop closure.

name: KISS-SLAM
summary: LiDAR SLAM that adds loop closure and pose-graph optimization on top of KISS-ICP odometry.
why_it_matters: Full LiDAR SLAM with the same low-configuration philosophy.
hackathon_notes: Pip-installable; quick to demo on outdoor bags.

name: MapClosures
summary: Loop-closure detection using bird's-eye-view density images of local LiDAR maps.
why_it_matters: Sensor-agnostic loop closure that plugs into any LiDAR odometry.
hackathon_notes: Python bindings via pip.

name: RKO-LIO
summary: LiDAR-inertial odometry aiming to work without sensor-specific modelling or heavy tuning.
why_it_matters: Recent (2025-2026) LIO from the KISS-ICP group; good for unknown hardware.
hackathon_notes: Check README for pip/ROS 2 usage; similar ergonomics to KISS-ICP.

name: LeGO-LOAM
summary: Lightweight ground-optimized LiDAR odometry and mapping that segments ground to speed up feature extraction on UGVs.
why_it_matters: Classic UGV LiDAR SLAM for rough terrain on modest compute.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1 only, unmaintained, tuned for Velodyne VLP-16. Use LIO-SAM or KISS-ICP instead unless reproducing baselines.

name: Cartographer
summary: Real-time 2D and 3D SLAM with submaps and branch-and-bound loop closure across many sensor configurations.
why_it_matters: Widely deployed 2D LiDAR SLAM for indoor and warehouse robots.
hackathon_notes: Project is in maintenance mode with little activity. Still available via ROS packages and works for 2D indoor mapping.

name: GLIM
summary: Versatile point-cloud localization and mapping framework with GPU-accelerated factor graphs, supporting many range sensors and optional IMU.
why_it_matters: Modern, maintained 3D mapping with GPU speedups and an extensible module system.
hackathon_notes: Prebuilt packages exist for ROS 2; GPU optional but recommended.

name: fast_gicp
summary: Collection of fast GICP and VGICP point-cloud registration implementations, multithreaded and CUDA.
why_it_matters: Fast scan registration building block used by many LiDAR and radar SLAM systems.
hackathon_notes: Successor library small_gicp is more actively maintained.

name: small_gicp
summary: Efficient, parallel point-cloud registration library (GICP, ICP variants) with C++ and Python APIs.
why_it_matters: Pip-installable registration to build your own LiDAR odometry or map-based relocalization fast.
hackathon_notes: `pip install small_gicp`; good for scan-to-map localization prototypes.

name: Faster-LIO
summary: Lightweight tightly coupled LiDAR-inertial odometry using parallel sparse incremental voxels instead of a k-d tree.
why_it_matters: Faster variant of the FAST-LIO design for constrained compute.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1; same config style as FAST-LIO.

name: DLIO
summary: Lightweight LiDAR-inertial odometry with coarse-to-fine continuous-time motion correction (ICRA 2023).
why_it_matters: Accurate and compute-light LIO for aerial and ground robots.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1 main; check community ROS 2 forks.

name: FAST_LIO_LOCALIZATION
summary: Relocalization in a prebuilt map using FAST-LIO odometry plus global scan-to-map registration.
why_it_matters: Localize in a map you surveyed earlier, the standard pattern for GNSS-denied ground ops in known areas.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1; build a map with FAST-LIO first, then localize. Needs a rough initial pose.

name: Scan Context
summary: LiDAR global place descriptor for loop detection and relocalization (backup of the original IRAP KAIST repo).
why_it_matters: Simple, widely used LiDAR loop-closure descriptor; plugs into most LiDAR SLAM.
hackathon_notes: Header-only style C++; SC-LIO-SAM shows integration.

name: SC-LIO-SAM
summary: LIO-SAM combined with Scan Context loop closure for more reliable large-scale LiDAR-inertial SLAM.
why_it_matters: Practical recipe for adding a global descriptor to an existing LIO.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1; same setup as LIO-SAM.

name: STD
summary: Stable Triangle Descriptor for 3D point-cloud place recognition and loop closure.
why_it_matters: Works with solid-state LiDARs and small fields of view where Scan Context struggles.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1 demos; integrates with FAST-LIO.

name: TEASER++
summary: Certifiable, outlier-robust point-cloud registration library with C++, Python and MATLAB bindings.
why_it_matters: Global registration that tolerates extreme outlier rates, useful for map-to-map alignment and relocalization.
hackathon_notes: Needs correspondences (e.g. FPFH) as input; Python bindings make it quick to prototype.

name: Quatro
summary: Fast, robust global registration for terrestrial robots that assumes near-planar motion to cut degrees of freedom.
why_it_matters: Faster global relocalization for ground vehicles.
hackathon_notes: Smaller research codebase; pair with KISS-ICP.

name: MIMOSA
summary: Tightly coupled sliding-window factor-graph fusion of IMU with LiDAR (geometric and photometric), radar radial-speed factors and external odometry such as VIO.
why_it_matters: From the group behind DARPA SubT field robots; relevant to smoke/dark/dust scenarios.
hackathon_notes: ROS Noetic; publishes nav_msgs/Odometry. Radar factor lets you keep velocity constraints when LiDAR is blinded by dust or smoke.

name: livox_ros_driver2
summary: ROS 1/ROS 2 driver for Livox LiDARs such as Mid-360 and HAP.
why_it_matters: Mid-360 is a common cheap LiDAR for drones; you need this driver to feed FAST-LIO and friends.
hackathon_notes: Build with the Livox SDK2; set the custom message format expected by FAST-LIO.

name: hdl_graph_slam
summary: 3D LiDAR graph SLAM with NDT/GICP scan matching odometry, loop detection and optional GPS, IMU and floor-plane constraints.
why_it_matters: Simple, hackable graph SLAM that 4DRadarSLAM and others build on; GPS constraints make it handy for mixed GNSS/denied runs.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1; GLIM is the author's newer framework.

name: Kimera-Distributed
summary: Distributed back end of Kimera-Multi handling inter-robot loop closures and distributed optimization.
why_it_matters: Reusable distributed SLAM back end.
hackathon_notes: Used through Kimera-Multi.

name: DPGO
summary: Distributed pose-graph optimization library with certifiably correct solutions for multi-robot SLAM.
why_it_matters: Solver core for decentralized multi-robot SLAM.
hackathon_notes: Library only; feed it pose graphs from each robot.

name: Swarm-SLAM
summary: ROS 2 decentralized collaborative SLAM supporting LiDAR, stereo and RGB-D, with sparse inter-robot communication.
why_it_matters: Designed for bandwidth-limited swarms, a realistic constraint under jamming.
hackathon_notes: ROS 2; experiments run on recorded multi-robot datasets. Pick one sensor type to start.

name: COVINS / COVINS-G
summary: Centralized collaborative visual-inertial SLAM where agents run VIO and a server merges maps; COVINS-G is VIO-front-end agnostic.
why_it_matters: Pattern for drones sharing maps through a ground station.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1 + Docker; COVINS-G can take poses from any VIO such as OpenVINS.

name: 14 Lectures on Visual SLAM (English)
summary: English edition of Gao Xiang's open textbook on visual SLAM, from geometry and Lie groups to back-end optimization.
why_it_matters: Best free practical intro for a team ramping up on SLAM in a weekend.
hackathon_notes: PDF and code exercises (slambook2 repo).

title: Vision-based GNSS-Free Localization for UAVs in the Wild
summary: Proposes matching drone camera frames to open satellite imagery with learned feature matching to get absolute position without GNSS, evaluated on flights over non-urban areas.
key_takeaways: Satellite tiles + learned matcher is a workable visual GPS baseline
Failure cases cluster over low-texture and changed terrain

title: AnyLoc: Towards Universal Visual Place Recognition
summary: Shows that unsupervised aggregation of foundation-model (DINOv2) features gives place recognition that generalizes across domains including aerial imagery, without VPR-specific training.
key_takeaways: Foundation features + VLAD work training-free
Aerial domain included in the evaluation

title: Exploring the best way for UAV visual localization under Low-altitude Multi-view Observation Condition: a Benchmark
summary: Builds a benchmark for low-altitude, oblique-view UAV absolute visual localization and systematically compares retrieval, matching and refinement choices.
key_takeaways: Low-altitude oblique views are much harder than nadir
Gives evidence for picking retrieval/matcher combos

title: UAV-VisLoc: A Large-scale Dataset for UAV Visual Localization
summary: Introduces a dataset of real UAV flight images paired with satellite maps over varied terrain for evaluating UAV visual localization.
key_takeaways: Real flights with ground truth
Covers terrain types beyond cities

title: Long-range UAV Thermal Geo-localization with Satellite Imagery
summary: Matches night-time UAV thermal imagery to satellite RGB maps using domain adaptation to cope with scarce paired thermal-satellite data; releases code and a nighttime dataset.
key_takeaways: Night visual GPS is possible via thermal-to-RGB matching
Domain adaptation offsets missing paired data

title: STHN: Deep Homography Estimation for UAV Thermal Geo-localization with Satellite Imagery
summary: Refines thermal-to-satellite localization with learned homography estimation for precise alignment.
key_takeaways: Coarse-to-fine: retrieval then homography

title: UASTHN: Uncertainty-Aware Deep Homography Estimation for UAV Satellite-Thermal Geo-localization
summary: Adds uncertainty estimation to satellite-thermal homography so a navigation filter can weight or reject visual fixes.
key_takeaways: Uncertainty makes visual fixes filter-ready

title: University-1652: A Multi-view Multi-source Benchmark for Drone-based Geo-localization
summary: Introduces the drone/satellite/ground benchmark that most drone cross-view geo-localization work evaluates on.
key_takeaways: Defines drone->satellite and satellite->drone retrieval tasks
