title: Visual Navigation for Flying Robots (TUM, 2013)
summary: Award-winning TUM lecture on making quadrotors navigate with cameras: 3D geometry, sensors, state estimation, visual motion estimation, SLAM, dense reconstruction, planning and exploration. Each lecture has slides and a recorded video.
key_takeaways: Compact quadrotor-centric syllabus
Bridges control, estimation and visual SLAM

title: Autonomous Navigation for Flying Robots (TUM edX, AUTONAVx)
summary: MOOC version of the TUM flying-robots lecture with lecture videos and browser-based Python exercises on quadrotor state estimation, Kalman filtering, control and visual navigation.
key_takeaways: Lighter-weight than the full lecture
Python exercise format is easy to adapt

title: Kalman and Bayesian Filters in Python
summary: Free interactive book as Jupyter notebooks: g-h filters, discrete Bayes, univariate and multivariate Kalman filters, EKF, UKF, particle filters and smoothers, all with runnable code built on the companion FilterPy library.
key_takeaways: Intuition-first, code-first; ideal for teammates new to filtering
Notebooks run in Binder or locally
FilterPy gives drop-in KF/EKF/UKF classes for prototypes

title: Kalman Filter Tutorial (kalmanfilter.net)
summary: Free web tutorial deriving the Kalman filter through worked numerical examples (alpha-beta filter, 1D and multidimensional KF, EKF, UKF), written for engineers who want the equations without heavy theory.
key_takeaways: Numeric step-by-step examples you can check by hand
Good companion to Labbe for tracking problems

title: SLAM Handbook: From Localization and Mapping to Spatial Intelligence
summary: Community-written handbook released in three parts during 2024-2025 and published by Cambridge University Press; the free PDF is mirrored on the editors' project page. Covers factor graphs, Lie groups, robust estimation, certifiable methods, visual/LiDAR/radar/event-based SLAM, and learned spatial representations.
key_takeaways: Most current one-stop reference on SLAM (2025)
Chapters on non-visual sensors such as radar
Free PDF; GitHub repo tracks newest release
Single up-to-date reference spanning classic estimation and learned methods
Free chapter PDFs on GitHub

title: SLAM toolbox for Matlab (EKF-SLAM teaching code)
summary: Solà's Matlab EKF-SLAM toolbox, used as teaching material for his SLAM courses: modular robots, sensors, landmark parameterizations (including inverse-depth points and lines) and graph-SLAM variants. Old but clear code for learning.
key_takeaways: Readable reference implementation of EKF-SLAM
Shows landmark parameterization trade-offs

title: 14 Lectures on Visual SLAM: From Theory to Practice
summary: English translation of the popular Chinese visual SLAM textbook, from rigid-body motion and Lie algebra through camera models, nonlinear optimization, feature/direct VO, backend optimization, loop closure and dense mapping, each with C++ examples.
key_takeaways: Code-heavy: every chapter compiles
Good bridge from theory to ORB-SLAM-style systems

title: State Estimation and Localization for Self-Driving Cars (Coursera)
summary: Course 2 of the UofT Self-Driving Cars specialization: least squares, KF/EKF/ES-EKF/UKF, IMU and GNSS sensor models, LiDAR scan matching with ICP, culminating in an error-state EKF that fuses IMU, GNSS and LiDAR on CARLA data.
key_takeaways: Final project is a ready template for GNSS/IMU/LiDAR fusion
Explicit error-state EKF derivation
Free to audit

title: Self-Driving Cars Specialization (University of Toronto)
summary: Four-course specialization covering vehicle dynamics and control, state estimation and localization, visual perception, and motion planning, using the CARLA simulator for assignments.
key_takeaways: End-to-end autonomy pipeline in one program
CARLA-based assignments transfer to hackathon sims

title: GPS: An Introduction to Satellite Navigation, with an interactive Worldwide Laboratory using Smartphones
summary: Stanford MOOC (originally on Coursera) now freely available as a long video series: how GPS works, pseudoranges, orbits and signals, receiver design, assisted GPS and the future of GNSS, with smartphone-based labs.
key_takeaways: Best intro to pseudoranges and receiver basics
Smartphone labs pair with Android raw GNSS measurements

title: Sensor Fusion and Non-linear Filtering for Automotive Systems (edX)
summary: Self-paced edX course on Bayesian filtering: state-space and motion/measurement models, Kalman filter, EKF/UKF/CKF, and particle filters, with Matlab assignments building a personal filtering toolbox.
key_takeaways: Rigorous but practical nonlinear filtering
Pairs with Chalmers' multi-object tracking course

title: Multi-Object Tracking for Automotive Systems (edX)
summary: edX course on single- and multi-object tracking: data association, GNN/JPDA/MHT, random finite sets and PMBM filters, with Matlab assignments. Relevant for situational awareness and C-UAS track management.
key_takeaways: Modern RFS/PMBM trackers explained
Direct use for radar/EO track fusion

title: Artificial Intelligence for Robotics (Udacity CS373)
summary: Free classic course by Sebastian Thrun programming robot localization (histogram filter, Kalman filter, particle filter), search/planning, PID control and GraphSLAM in Python.
key_takeaways: Gentle, code-along intro to localization filters
Particle-filter lesson is a 1-hour hackathon primer

title: Understanding Sensor Fusion and Tracking (MATLAB Tech Talks)
summary: Short video series on sensor fusion for autonomous systems: what sensor fusion is, IMU/magnetometer orientation estimation, fusing GPS and IMU for pose with an asynchronous EKF, single- and multi-object tracking, and track-level fusion.
key_takeaways: Clear 10-15 minute visual explanations
GPS+IMU episode maps directly to a nav-filter build

title: Stanford PNT Symposium 2025 (19th annual)
authors: Stanford Center for Position, Navigation and Time
summary: Annual Stanford SCPNT symposium page (8-9 October 2025) with the agenda and links to recorded student talks (Day 1) and invited speaker talks (Day 2), plus downloadable slides for many presentations.
key_takeaways: Current state of GNSS integrity, resilience and alt-PNT from leading labs
Student talks are a good source of fresh project ideas

title: 2025 PNT Symposium - Day 2 Invited Speaker Presentation Videos
summary: Video album of invited speaker talks from the 2025 Stanford PNT Symposium, featuring speakers such as Brad Parkinson and Jade Morton.
key_takeaways: Primary-source talks on the direction of GPS and resilient PNT

title: Stanford PNT Symposium 2024 (18th annual)
summary: Page for the 28-29 October 2024 symposium with agenda, student and invited-speaker video albums, and slides; topics span GNSS, inertial sensing, timing and alternative navigation.
key_takeaways: Year-over-year view of resilient PNT research
Slides downloadable for many talks

title: SCPNT Photo and Video Gallery (PNT Symposium recordings archive)
summary: Archive index of Stanford PNT Symposium recordings going back to 2007, organised by year into student and invited-speaker albums.
key_takeaways: Deep back-catalogue of GNSS and PNT talks

title: ION GNSS+ Tutorials
summary: Pre-conference tutorial programme of ION GNSS+, the main annual GNSS technical meeting: half-day in-depth courses by field experts on topics such as GNSS signals, receivers, PPP/RTK, inertial integration and interference.
key_takeaways: Expert-taught deep dives; topics change yearly
Paid add-on to conference registration

title: ION GNSS+ Short Courses (GPS/GNSS 101 and more)
summary: Short courses run at ION GNSS+ for registered attendees, including a GPS/GNSS 101 course taught by John Raquet and a space applications of GNSS course by Penina Axelrad.
key_takeaways: Fast fundamentals refresh for newcomers attending ION GNSS+

title: ION Online Tutorial: The Basics of Satellite Navigation
summary: ION's free online tutorial introducing satellite navigation fundamentals: trilateration with pseudoranges, clocks, signals, error sources and augmentation.
key_takeaways: Free, short, authoritative intro

title: ION Webinar Series (archive and YouTube recordings)
summary: Running ION webinar programme with summary pages per talk and a YouTube playlist of past recordings (youtube.com/playlist?list=PLPiP0PPIY2x4k1OemLZH8_OJPyLjGLYFY). Topics include GNSS spoofing and jamming, LEO PNT, signals of opportunity, quantum sensors and GNSS-denied robotics.
key_takeaways: Hour-long talks from active researchers, free
Strong coverage of spoofing detection and LEO PNT

title: First results from three years of GNSS interference monitoring from low Earth orbit
summary: UT Radionavigation Lab results from detecting and geolocating terrestrial GNSS jammers using receivers on LEO satellites, revealing persistent interference hotspots in conflict regions.
key_takeaways: Space-based RFI monitoring is practical
Maps of jamming hotspots tied to conflict zones

title: Unveiling Starlink for PNT
summary: Presents work on exploiting Starlink downlink signals for opportunistic positioning, including signal structure discovery and Doppler/pseudorange-based navigation results.
key_takeaways: Starlink can serve as an alt-PNT source without operator cooperation

title: Navigation using carrier Doppler shift from a LEO constellation: TRANSIT on steroids
summary: Analysis of Doppler-only positioning from large LEO constellations, revisiting the TRANSIT concept with modern megaconstellations and quantifying achievable accuracy.
key_takeaways: Doppler positioning theory for LEO PNT

title: Implementation and Accuracy of Doppler Navigation with LEO Satellites
summary: Implementation-focused talk on navigating with Doppler measurements from LEO satellites and the accuracy achieved in practice.
key_takeaways: Practical error budget for LEO Doppler nav

title: Detecting GNSS Jamming and Spoofing on Android Devices
summary: Shows how Android raw GNSS measurements (AGC, C/N0, pseudoranges) can flag jamming and spoofing on commodity phones.
key_takeaways: Phones can be cheap distributed interference sensors

title: Results on GNSS Spoofing Mitigation Using Multiple Receivers
summary: Spoofing detection and mitigation using several spatially separated receivers, exploiting the fact that a single spoofer produces geometrically inconsistent measurements.
key_takeaways: Multi-antenna/multi-receiver consistency checks

title: GNSS Spoofing Detection through Spatial Processing
summary: Stanford work on detecting spoofing from spatial signal characteristics (angle-of-arrival consistency) using antenna motion or arrays.
key_takeaways: Direction-of-arrival is a strong spoofing discriminator

title: Robust Interference Mitigation in GNSS Snapshot Receivers
summary: Interference mitigation techniques adapted to snapshot (short-capture) GNSS receivers used in low-power and IoT devices.
key_takeaways: Snapshot receivers need different mitigation than tracking receivers

title: A Robust Approach to Vision-Based Terrain-Aided Localization
summary: Vision-based terrain-aided localization for aircraft, matching onboard imagery against terrain/map references as a GNSS-independent position source.
key_takeaways: Map-matching as a GNSS-denied position fix

title: Cooperative Localization for GNSS-Denied Subterranean Navigation: A UAV-UGV Team Approach
summary: West Virginia University work on UAV and UGV teams sharing ranging and odometry to localize jointly in GNSS-denied underground environments.
key_takeaways: Cooperative ranging reduces drift in heterogeneous teams

title: Relative navigation of fixed-wing aircraft in GPS-denied environments
summary: AFRL perspective on relative navigation for fixed-wing aircraft without GPS, keeping estimation consistent by working in a relative frame with periodic global updates.
key_takeaways: Relative navigation frames tame unobservable global drift

title: Quantum Sensors for Navigation, From Physics to Field Deployment
summary: Overview of quantum sensing for navigation (atom interferometers, quantum magnetometers, clocks) and what it takes to move them from lab to field.
key_takeaways: Realistic timeline for quantum inertial and magnetic nav

title: Should It Be TPN? Prioritizing Timing in Positioning and Navigation
summary: Webinar arguing for timing as the foundation of resilient PNT, covering precision terrestrial time distribution and timing/positioning from current and future LEO constellations.
key_takeaways: Timing resilience underpins telecom and power grid
LEO as a timing source

title: LTE Receiver Design and Multipath Analysis for Navigation in Urban Environments
summary: Design of a software receiver that extracts navigation observables from cellular LTE signals and analysis of multipath effects in urban settings.
key_takeaways: Cellular signals of opportunity are viable in cities

title: Resilience Monitoring for Multi-Filter All-Source Navigation Framework With Assurance
summary: AFIT research on all-source navigation that runs multiple filters and monitors sensor integrity to detect and isolate faulty or spoofed inputs.
key_takeaways: Plug-and-play all-source nav with integrity monitoring

title: When GNSS fails, what will you do? MarRINav!
summary: UK maritime resilient navigation study (MarRINav) on backups for GNSS at sea, including eLoran and R-Mode style terrestrial systems; co-sponsored by the RNT Foundation.
key_takeaways: Maritime PNT backup architecture options

title: How to fool a GPS (TEDxAustin)
summary: Accessible TEDx talk from the head of UT Austin's Radionavigation Lab on GPS jamming and spoofing and why civil GPS is trivially counterfeitable, given around the time of his lab's drone and yacht spoofing demonstrations.
key_takeaways: Why unauthenticated civil GNSS is a systemic risk
Good opener for a resilient-PNT pitch

title: UT Austin Radionavigation Laboratory (talks, papers, news)
summary: Lab site of Todd Humphreys' group, indexing talks, briefings and papers on GNSS spoofing detection, LEO interference monitoring, Starlink-based PNT and precise automotive positioning.
key_takeaways: Hub for Humphreys' talks on spoofing and LEO PNT
Papers on spoofing detection are linked from here

title: Ad Astra: Navigation with Megaconstellation LEO Satellites (GRASP on Robotics)
summary: UPenn GRASP seminar by Zak Kassas on opportunistic PNT from Starlink, OneWeb and other LEO megaconstellations, addressing unknown signal structure, poor ephemerides and clock instability with his STAN (simultaneous tracking and navigation) framework validated on ground and aerial vehicles.
key_takeaways: LEO signals of opportunity as a GNSS backup
Covers SDR receiver design to navigation filter

title: Low-cost GPS simulator: GPS spoofing by SDR (DEF CON 23)
summary: DEF CON 23 talk showing that open-source tools and cheap SDRs can generate counterfeit GPS L1 signals that fool phones and a consumer drone; the speakers end with defensive advice such as multi-constellation positioning and spoofing detection in chipsets.
key_takeaways: Shows how low the barrier to civil GPS spoofing is
Motivates detection and multi-source fusion in any drone build

title: Who cares about the Baltic Jammer? Terrestrial Navigation in the Baltic Sea Region (39C3)
summary: 39th Chaos Communication Congress talk from DLR researchers on R-Mode, a terrestrial maritime navigation backup built on existing radio beacons and coastal infrastructure, tested in the heavily jammed Baltic. Covers real-world jamming impacts, transmitter/receiver build-out and the path from research to critical infrastructure.
key_takeaways: Concrete view of Baltic jamming/spoofing effects on ships, aircraft, timing
Terrestrial backups as an alternative to space-based ones

title: Detect GNSS jamming and spoofing (Android developer guide)
summary: Android developer documentation on the platform APIs and signals that apps can use to detect GNSS jamming and spoofing on phones.
key_takeaways: Phone-based interference sensing for a hackathon prototype
No custom hardware needed

title: Results Jammertest 2025 - Resilient GNSS in an Era of Rising Jamming & Spoofing (webinar)
summary: On-demand vendor webinar reviewing receiver behaviour during the high-power interference trials of Jammertest 2025 in Norway, with speakers from Septentrio, the GPS Innovation Alliance and drone maker UVify.
key_takeaways: Field results under interference levels like Baltic/Eastern Europe
Vendor view; treat claims accordingly

title: Jamming, spoofing and secure positioning: Jammertest insights (u-blox webinar)
summary: On-demand u-blox webinar on what multi-band receiver testing at Jammertest revealed about positioning continuity under interference and hybrid spoofing detection.
key_takeaways: Multi-band receivers and spoofing detection in mass-market chips

title: GNSS vulnerabilities explained (PolicyTracker Spectrum Podcast)
summary: Spectrum-policy podcast episode with PNT consultant Logan Scott on GNSS jamming, spoofing, adjacent-band interference and mitigations, and the global rise in spoofing incidents affecting aviation.
key_takeaways: Policy and spectrum angle on GNSS interference

title: From the Crows' Nest - growing threats to GPS/GNSS (Dana Goward)
summary: Episode of the Association of Old Crows electronic warfare podcast in which RNT Foundation president Dana Goward discusses threats to GPS and the case for terrestrial and other backups.
key_takeaways: EW-community framing of PNT resilience

title: Dana A. Goward on Geospatial FM podcast (RNT Foundation)
summary: RNT Foundation post linking Dana Goward's Geospatial FM podcast appearance on GPS vulnerability and national PNT resilience policy.
key_takeaways: Advocacy perspective on eLoran and PNT backups

title: EUDIS Defence Hackathon, 3rd edition (with BraveTech EU)
summary: EU defence hackathon (17-19 October 2025, eight locations) with challenges on protecting space assets, space for defence (including navigation and coordination) and sovereign aerospace including drone countermeasures; a recorded pre-hackathon webinar is on YouTube (watch?v=gLrCkk6XEuY).
key_takeaways: Shows how EU frames navigation and C-UAS challenge statements
Pre-hackathon webinar recording available

title: Ukraine's DefTech at the End of 2025: From Drone Mass to Systems Warfare
summary: Analysis of Ukraine's defence-tech ecosystem at the end of 2025, noting that GNSS-denied operation is now the norm and expecting broad adoption of radio-beacon, visual and fused alternative navigation in 2026.
key_takeaways: GNSS denial is a baseline requirement in current conflict
Context for prioritising alt-nav in hackathon scope

title: Navigating Using GPS Localization (Nav2 tutorial)
summary: Nav2 tutorial on outdoor navigation with GPS: fusing GNSS, IMU and odometry with robot_localization's navsat_transform, configuring Nav2 for GPS waypoints, and demonstrating it in Gazebo.
key_takeaways: Shortest working path to GPS waypoint following on a ROS 2 robot
Shows datum and frame setup that trips people up

title: ROSCon UK 2025 - State Estimation for Mobile Robotics Workshop
summary: Hands-on workshop material comparing two ROS 2 state-estimation approaches: Kalman filtering with robot_localization (EKF/UKF, covariance tuning, frames, rate handling) and factor-graph fixed-lag smoothing with fuse. Exercises and solutions are in a public repo.
key_takeaways: Filter vs smoother trade-offs with runnable exercises
Directly reusable configs for IMU/odom/GPS fusion

title: Nav2 first-time robot setup: Odometry and robot_localization
summary: Setup guide for fusing wheel odometry and IMU with robot_localization's EKF to produce the odom frame Nav2 expects.
key_takeaways: Minimal correct EKF config for a new robot

title: Nav2 ROSCon Talks index
summary: Index of ROSCon talks by Nav2 developers and the community (Vimeo links), including SLAM Toolbox and large-scale indoor mapping talks.
key_takeaways: Curated entry point into ROSCon navigation videos

title: robot_localization package documentation
summary: Documentation for the widely used ROS EKF/UKF state estimation package, including state-estimation node configuration, sensor integration, and navsat_transform for GPS.
key_takeaways: Explains covariance and frame conventions in depth
navsat_transform page is essential for GPS fusion

title: ROSCon 2023 videos and slides
summary: Announcement and index of ROSCon 2023 recordings and slides, including navigation talks such as bidirectional navigation with Nav2 and localization on 3D mesh surfaces.
key_takeaways: One place to find localization/navigation ROSCon talks

title: ROSCon 2024 (Odense) programme and recordings
summary: ROSCon 2024 site with the programme and links to recorded talks, including localization talks such as Ekumen's Beluga particle-filter localization library.
key_takeaways: Recent ROS 2 localization tooling talks

title: PX4 Developer Summit (talks and recordings)
summary: Annual PX4 developer conference; recordings are posted on the PX4 YouTube channel. The 2025 Atlanta programme included an EKF2 session on handling multiple data sources with 'reset by fusion' rather than hard resets.
key_takeaways: Primary source on EKF2 design changes
Talks on external vision/non-GNSS aiding in PX4

title: PX4 Autopilot YouTube channel
summary: Official channel with PX4 Developer Summit recordings, dev calls and feature demos.
key_takeaways: Search 'EKF2' for estimator deep dives

title: PX4 Simulation (Gazebo, SITL) documentation
summary: How to run PX4 software-in-the-loop with Gazebo and other simulators, including multi-vehicle setups and connecting ROS 2 and ground stations.
key_takeaways: Fastest way to test nav changes without hardware
Start here for PX4 SITL
Covers Gazebo, jMAVSim and community sims

title: Gazebo documentation and tutorials
summary: Official Gazebo (gz) docs and tutorials: building worlds, sensors (IMU, GPS/NavSat, cameras, LiDAR), ROS 2 bridging and plugins.
key_takeaways: NavSat and IMU sensors enable GNSS-denied scenario testing

title: Isaac ROS Visual SLAM documentation
summary: Docs and quickstarts for NVIDIA's GPU-accelerated stereo visual-inertial odometry and SLAM package for ROS 2 on Jetson, including tutorials with Isaac Sim and RealSense cameras.
key_takeaways: Real-time VIO on Jetson with minimal setup
Isaac Sim tutorials for testing without hardware

title: OpenVINS documentation
authors: Robot Perception and Navigation Group, University of Delaware
summary: Documentation for the OpenVINS MSCKF-based visual-inertial estimator, including derivations of the propagation and update steps, calibration, evaluation tooling and ROS usage.
key_takeaways: Doubles as a VIO textbook with derivations
Evaluation tools for comparing trajectories

title: Kalibr wiki: camera-IMU calibration tutorials
summary: Wiki for Kalibr covering multi-camera, camera-IMU and rolling-shutter calibration, target generation and data collection practice.
key_takeaways: Bad calibration ruins VIO; this is the standard workflow

title: GNSS-SDR tutorials
summary: Tutorials for the open-source GNSS-SDR software receiver: signal acquisition and tracking, configuring front ends, processing recorded IQ files, and generating observables and PVT.
key_takeaways: Learn receiver internals with real IQ data
Base for interference-detection experiments

title: Hilti SLAM Challenge
summary: SLAM benchmark challenge with datasets from handheld and robot-mounted multi-sensor rigs in construction sites and buildings, run with an associated ICRA workshop and public leaderboard.
key_takeaways: Hard GNSS-denied indoor sequences with accurate ground truth
Sensors: lidar, cameras, IMU
GNSS-denied indoor

title: Long-Term Visual Localization benchmark
summary: Benchmark and workshop series for 6-DoF visual localization under changing conditions (day/night, seasons), with standard datasets and an evaluation server.
key_takeaways: Standard evaluation for map-based visual relocalization

title: Image Matching: Local Features & Beyond (CVPR workshop)
summary: Recurring CVPR workshop and Kaggle challenge on feature matching and structure-from-motion, with invited talks and recordings, covering the matchers used in visual geolocalization and VIO.
key_takeaways: State of the art in learned matchers (SuperPoint/LightGlue family)

title: From Sea to Space: Advancing Perception in Harsh Domains (ICRA 2026 workshop)
summary: ICRA 2026 (Vienna) workshop on perception for underwater, space and terrestrial field robots, including localization and mapping in degraded sensing, GPS-denied global localization, novel sensors (sonar, radar, thermal, event) and edge-efficient perception.
key_takeaways: Cross-domain view of degraded-sensing localization
Speaker list points to active groups

title: ERF26 workshop: Innovation and developments in robotic GNSS-denied localisation for inspection & maintenance
summary: European Robotics Forum 2026 workshop (Stavanger) organised by SINTEF on GNSS-denied robot localisation in indoor, offshore, underground and urban-canyon settings, bringing together researchers, vendors and end users.
key_takeaways: Industry-side view of deployable GNSS-denied localisation

title: Nav2 Documentation
summary: Official Nav2 documentation: concepts, configuration guides for every planner/controller/costmap plugin, tuning guide and tutorials including GPS-based navigation.
key_takeaways: Tuning guide explains planner/controller trade-offs
Tutorials cover writing custom plugins and outdoor GPS waypoints

title: Nav2 ROSCon Talks (index)
summary: Curated index of ROSCon talks by the Nav2 team and community from 2018 onward, covering features such as Smac planners and the MPPI controller plus tuning and deployment advice.
key_takeaways: Single entry point for Nav2 conference talks
Talks on MPPI and Smac planners explain design rationale

title: The Marathon 2: A Navigation System
summary: Paper introducing Nav2: behavior-tree based navigation architecture for ROS 2, its design choices and a long-duration campus deployment test.
key_takeaways: Explains why Nav2 uses behavior trees and lifecycle nodes
Describes long-running real-world validation

title: From the Desks of ROS Maintainers: A Survey of Modern & Capable Mobile Robotics Algorithms in the Robot Operating System 2
summary: Survey by ROS maintainers of the mobile robotics algorithms available in ROS 2: localization, SLAM, planning, control and perception packages, with their maturity and use.
key_takeaways: Map of which ROS 2 packages are production-ready
Good orientation before choosing a localization or planning stack

title: The Open Motion Planning Library (OMPL) website
summary: Official OMPL documentation with planner catalogue, tutorials, Python binding guide and benchmarking tools.
key_takeaways: Tutorials show how to define state spaces and validity checkers
Built-in benchmarking compares planners on your problem

title: EGO-Planner: An ESDF-free Gradient-based Local Planner for Quadrotors
summary: Introduces a local planner that avoids building a full Euclidean signed distance field, computing collision penalties only from obstacles the trajectory intersects, cutting onboard compute.
key_takeaways: ESDF-free collision cost reduces mapping overhead
Fits small onboard computers for agile flight

title: Robust and Efficient Quadrotor Trajectory Generation for Fast Autonomous Flight
summary: Fast-Planner paper: kinodynamic path search front-end plus B-spline optimization and time adjustment for fast quadrotor flight in unknown environments.
key_takeaways: Front-end/back-end split is the template many later planners follow

title: Aerostack2: A Software Framework for Developing Multi-robot Aerial Systems
summary: Describes the Aerostack2 ROS 2 architecture for aerial robotics: platform abstraction, behaviors, mission specification and multi-robot support.
key_takeaways: Platform abstraction lets the same mission run on several autopilots and simulators

title: PlanSys2: A Planning System Framework for ROS2
summary: Presents PlanSys2, a PDDL planning and execution framework for ROS 2 that compiles plans into behavior trees and supports multi-robot execution.
key_takeaways: Shows how symbolic task planning connects to Nav2 actions

title: Fields2Cover: An open-source coverage path planning library for unmanned agricultural vehicles
summary: Paper behind the Fields2Cover library: modular coverage pipeline (headlands, swaths, route ordering, path smoothing) and benchmark of its components.
key_takeaways: Coverage planning decomposes cleanly into swath generation, ordering and turning

title: Cursor-on-Target Message Router User's Guide
summary: MITRE guide describing Cursor-on-Target: the base Event schema (what, where, when), its mandatory fields, sub-schema extensions and the message router used to distribute CoT.
key_takeaways: CoT base event is deliberately terse with a small set of mandatory fields
Type strings follow a hierarchical code derived from MIL-STD-2525

title: Developer's Guide to Cursor on Target
summary: Introductory developer guide to CoT's objectives, message structure, implementation patterns and limitations.
key_takeaways: Explains the what/where/when design philosophy
Good primer before writing a CoT producer

title: cot-types: Collection of Cursor-on-Target types
summary: Community-compiled list of CoT type strings with mappings to other message formats, useful when choosing the 'type' attribute for tracks.
key_takeaways: Pick correct atom/friend/hostile type codes for your tracks

title: MIL-STD-2525D Joint Military Symbology
summary: US DoD standard defining military symbology (frames, icons, modifiers and the symbol identification code) for C2 displays. Revision E (2022) is current and sold through standards resellers; 2525D was published openly on jcs.mil.
key_takeaways: SIDC structure drives symbol rendering in milsymbol
Know which revision your consumers expect (2525C vs D/E codes differ)

title: TAK.gov - Team Awareness Kit portal
summary: Official TAK portal for ATAK/WinTAK/iTAK/TAK Server downloads, plugin SDKs and documentation; most materials require free registration.
key_takeaways: Register early - SDK and server downloads are behind an account

title: OpenTAKServer Documentation
summary: Installation and configuration docs for OpenTAKServer, including client enrollment, certificates and integrations.
key_takeaways: Step-by-step install on Ubuntu or Raspberry Pi

title: PyTAK documentation
summary: Docs and examples for PyTAK: configuration, transports (TCP/UDP/TLS/multicast) and writing CoT producers.
key_takeaways: Example scripts are a minimal template for pushing positions to TAK

title: The 1090 Megahertz Riddle: A Guide to Decoding Mode S and ADS-B Signals
summary: Open book explaining Mode S and ADS-B message structure, position decoding (CPR), Comm-B registers and Mode S surveillance, with pyModeS examples.
key_takeaways: CPR position decoding explained step by step
Covers enhanced surveillance fields beyond basic ADS-B

title: EUROCONTROL ASTERIX
summary: EUROCONTROL home of the ASTERIX surveillance data exchange format, with category specifications for radar, ADS-B, MLAT and system tracks.
key_takeaways: Categories (e.g. 048 radar, 021 ADS-B, 062 system tracks) define the binary layouts

title: SpatioTemporal Asset Catalog (STAC) specification
summary: Specification and ecosystem site for STAC, the common way to describe and search geospatial imagery and DEM assets.
key_takeaways: Public STAC APIs give key-free access to Sentinel-2 and Copernicus DEM

title: Copernicus DEM on AWS Open Data
summary: Registry entry for the Copernicus global DEM (GLO-30/GLO-90) hosted as cloud-optimized GeoTIFFs on AWS, freely accessible without an account.
key_takeaways: Global 30 m DEM as COGs - sample directly with rasterio
Good default terrain for terrain-referenced nav and planning

title: GeographicLib documentation
summary: Documentation and background on geodesics, map projections, geoid and gravity models implemented in GeographicLib, plus online calculators.
key_takeaways: Geoid undulation matters when comparing GNSS ellipsoid heights to DEM heights

title: The EuRoC MAV Dataset
summary: Stereo camera and IMU sequences from a micro aerial vehicle in an industrial hall and a Vicon room, with laser-tracker or motion-capture ground truth. The baseline benchmark for VIO.
key_takeaways: Sensors: stereo grayscale, IMU
Size class: small (GB range)
Use for first VIO sanity checks

title: KITTI Visual Odometry / SLAM Evaluation
summary: Driving sequences with stereo cameras, Velodyne lidar and GPS/IMU ground truth, plus a public leaderboard for odometry.
key_takeaways: Sensors: stereo, lidar, GPS/IMU
Size class: large
License: CC BY-NC-SA per site

title: KITTI-360
summary: Successor to KITTI with longer suburban drives, 360-degree perception sensors and dense annotations, with GPS/IMU poses.
key_takeaways: Sensors: perspective and fisheye cameras, lidar, GPS/IMU
Size class: very large

title: TUM VI Benchmark for Visual-Inertial Odometry
summary: Handheld stereo camera and IMU sequences indoors and outdoors with photometric calibration; ground truth only at start and end for long sequences.
key_takeaways: Sensors: stereo camera, IMU
Size class: medium
Good for long-term drift tests

title: TUM RGB-D SLAM Dataset and Benchmark
summary: Kinect RGB-D sequences with motion-capture ground truth and evaluation tools; the trajectory format is used widely by other tools.
key_takeaways: Sensors: RGB-D, accelerometer
Size class: medium

title: The UZH-FPV Drone Racing Dataset
summary: High-speed, aggressive FPV drone flights with camera, event camera and IMU data, with a leaderboard and recurring state estimation competitions.
key_takeaways: Sensors: cameras, event camera, IMU
Size class: medium
Hard for most VIO pipelines

title: The Zurich Urban Micro Aerial Vehicle Dataset
summary: Low-altitude urban MAV flight over streets with camera, IMU and GPS plus Google Street View imagery for appearance-based localization.
key_takeaways: Sensors: camera, IMU, GPS
Use for aerial-to-street-view localization

title: Newer College Dataset
summary: Handheld lidar plus stereo and multi-camera sequences around New College, Oxford, with precise ground truth from a survey-grade prior map. Now hosted on Hugging Face.
key_takeaways: Sensors: lidar, stereo, multi-camera, IMUs
Size class: large

title: Mid-Air Dataset
summary: Synthetic low-altitude quadcopter flights with RGB, depth, normals, semantics and stereo plus navigation sensors, each trajectory recorded under several weather and season conditions.
key_takeaways: Sensors (simulated): RGB, depth, IMU, GPS
Size class: large
Built on AirSim

title: TartanAir: A Dataset to Push the Limits of Visual SLAM
summary: Large synthetic dataset rendered in AirSim/Unreal environments with challenging lighting, weather and motion, with perfect ground truth for many modalities.
key_takeaways: Sensors (simulated): stereo, depth, flow, lidar, IMU
Size class: very large

title: SubT-MRS Dataset
summary: Multi-robot, multi-modal SLAM data in degraded environments - caves, tunnels, urban and off-road - with RGB, lidar, thermal and inertial sensing; used in ICCV SLAM challenges.
key_takeaways: Sensors: RGB, lidar, thermal, IMU
Domains: subterranean, off-road
Size class: large

title: DARPA SubT Reference Datasets
summary: Reference sensor datasets and artifact data released for the DARPA Subterranean Challenge, hosted on Bitbucket.
key_takeaways: Sensors: lidar, cameras, IMU from SubT-style robots
GNSS-denied underground

title: Oxford RobotCar Dataset
summary: Repeated drives of the same Oxford route over a year in all weather, with cameras, lidar and GPS/INS.
key_takeaways: Sensors: cameras, lidar, GPS/INS
Size class: very large
License: non-commercial per site

title: Oxford Radar RobotCar Dataset
summary: RobotCar route re-driven with a scanning FMCW radar plus lidars and cameras, for radar odometry and localization.
key_takeaways: Sensors: FMCW radar, lidar, cameras, GPS/INS
Size class: large

title: MulRan: Multimodal Range Dataset for Urban Place Recognition
summary: Urban sequences with radar and lidar for range-sensor place recognition and odometry.
key_takeaways: Sensors: radar, lidar, GPS, IMU
Size class: large

title: HeLiPR: Heterogeneous LiDAR Dataset for inter-LiDAR Place Recognition
summary: Same routes captured with Ouster, Aeva, Livox and Velodyne lidars to test place recognition across different lidar types.
key_takeaways: Sensors: four lidar types, IMU, GNSS/INS
Use for cross-sensor relocalization

title: Complex Urban Dataset
summary: Urban driving in dense city areas with lidar, stereo and navigation sensors where GNSS is degraded.
key_takeaways: Sensors: lidars, stereo, GNSS, IMU, wheel encoders
Size class: large

title: UrbanLoco: A Full Sensor Suite Dataset for Mapping and Localization in Urban Scenes
summary: Driving data from Hong Kong and California urban canyons with a full sensor suite, targeted at GNSS outliers and degraded localization.
key_takeaways: Sensors: lidar, cameras, GNSS, IMU
Focus: dense urban GNSS failure

title: The University of Michigan North Campus Long-Term Vision and LIDAR Dataset
summary: Segway robot sessions over many months on one campus with lidar, omnidirectional camera, GPS, IMU and odometry.
key_takeaways: Sensors: Velodyne HDL-32E, Ladybug3, GPS/RTK, IMU
Long-term change over seasons

title: MCD: Diverse Large-Scale Multi-Campus Dataset for Robot Perception
summary: Multi-campus sequences in Asia and Europe across seasons with two lidar types, stereo, IMUs, UWB and survey-grade prior maps.
key_takeaways: Sensors: lidar, stereo, IMU, UWB
Ground truth: continuous-time with prior maps

title: VECtor: A Versatile Event-Centric Benchmark for Multi-Sensor SLAM
summary: Hardware-synchronized event stereo, regular stereo, RGB-D, lidar and IMU across different motion and lighting, with 6-DoF ground truth.
key_takeaways: Sensors: event stereo, stereo, RGB-D, lidar, IMU

title: DSEC: A Stereo Event Camera Dataset for Driving Scenarios
summary: Stereo event and frame cameras plus lidar and RTK GNSS on a car, including night and challenging illumination.
key_takeaways: Sensors: stereo event, stereo RGB, lidar, RTK GNSS
Good for low-light perception

title: The Multi Vehicle Stereo Event Camera Dataset (MVSEC)
summary: Stereo event cameras with IMU, lidar and ground truth on several platforms including a hexacopter and a car.
key_takeaways: Sensors: stereo event, IMU, lidar, GPS
Platforms: drone, car, motorcycle, handheld

title: MARS-LVIG Dataset
summary: Aerial robot SLAM dataset for lidar-visual-inertial-GNSS fusion, including sequences with raw GNSS measurements under different lighting.
key_takeaways: Sensors: lidar, camera, IMU, GNSS (incl. raw)
Domain: aerial over large outdoor areas

title: ArduPilot SITL Simulator (Software in the Loop)
summary: Developer docs for running ArduPilot vehicles in SITL, connecting GCS and external simulators.
key_takeaways: sim_vehicle.py workflow
Lists supported external simulators

title: HoloOcean Documentation
summary: Install guide, sensor reference (sonar, DVL, IMU, depth) and examples for the HoloOcean underwater simulator.
key_takeaways: Covers sonar and DVL sensor configs
Multi-agent and acoustic comms examples

title: AirSim Documentation
summary: Docs for AirSim covering setup, APIs, sensor configuration and PX4/ArduPilot integration.
key_takeaways: Sensor settings via settings.json
Notes on the project's end of active development

title: Past, Present, and Future of Simultaneous Localization And Mapping: Towards the Robust-Perception Age
summary: Landmark survey that frames modern SLAM as factor-graph MAP estimation and discusses robustness, scalability, representations and open problems.
key_takeaways: Standard framing of front end vs back end
Robustness to outliers and long-term operation remain the hard problems

title: Visual-Inertial Navigation: A Concise Review
summary: Compact review of visual-inertial navigation: filtering vs optimization, observability, calibration and representative systems.
key_takeaways: Explains why MSCKF-style filters and sliding-window optimizers coexist
Observability and consistency drive estimator design

title: ORB-SLAM3: An Accurate Open-Source Library for Visual, Visual-Inertial and Multi-Map SLAM
summary: Describes ORB-SLAM3's tightly integrated visual-inertial SLAM, MAP-based IMU initialization and the multi-map Atlas that recovers from tracking loss.
key_takeaways: Multi-map atlas lets the system restart and later merge maps
Supports pinhole and fisheye models

title: VINS-Mono: A Robust and Versatile Monocular Visual-Inertial State Estimator
summary: Presents the VINS-Mono estimator: IMU preintegration, robust initialization, tightly coupled sliding-window optimization, relocalization and global pose graph.
key_takeaways: Monocular camera + IMU recovers metric scale
Initialization is a key practical component

title: FAST-LIO2: Fast Direct LiDAR-inertial Odometry
summary: Introduces direct registration of raw LiDAR points in an iterated Kalman filter with an incremental k-d tree map, avoiding hand-crafted feature extraction.
key_takeaways: Raw-point registration generalizes across LiDAR types
ikd-Tree enables efficient incremental mapping

title: LIO-SAM: Tightly-coupled Lidar Inertial Odometry via Smoothing and Mapping
summary: Formulates LiDAR-inertial odometry as factor-graph smoothing with IMU preintegration, LiDAR odometry, GPS and loop-closure factors.
key_takeaways: Factor graphs make it straightforward to add or drop GNSS
Keyframe-local scan matching keeps it real time

title: KISS-ICP: In Defense of Point-to-Point ICP -- Simple, Accurate, and Robust Registration If Done the Right Way
summary: Argues that a carefully engineered point-to-point ICP with motion compensation and adaptive thresholds matches far more complex LiDAR odometry across platforms.
key_takeaways: Few parameters, works across sensors and platforms
Strong baseline before reaching for complex pipelines

title: FAST-LIVO2: Fast, Direct LiDAR-Inertial-Visual Odometry
summary: Presents an error-state iterated Kalman filter that sequentially fuses LiDAR and image measurements against a shared voxel map, with exposure and plane-prior handling.
key_takeaways: Sequential updates handle LiDAR/camera dimension mismatch
Robust when one modality degrades

title: DROID-SLAM: Deep Visual SLAM for Monocular, Stereo, and RGB-D Cameras
summary: Learned SLAM that iteratively refines poses and depth through a differentiable dense bundle adjustment layer.
key_takeaways: Big robustness gains on hard sequences
GPU-heavy

title: MASt3R-SLAM: Real-Time Dense SLAM with 3D Reconstruction Priors
summary: Builds a real-time dense monocular SLAM system on the MASt3R two-view reconstruction prior, without assuming a fixed parametric camera model.
key_takeaways: 3D foundation models can serve as SLAM front ends
Works with uncalibrated video

title: Kimera: an Open-Source Library for Real-Time Metric-Semantic Localization and Mapping
summary: Describes the Kimera stack: VIO, robust pose-graph optimization, mesh reconstruction and semantic mapping in one open library.
key_takeaways: Metric-semantic maps on CPU in real time
Modular: VIO, RPGO, mesher, semantics

title: Kimera-Multi: Robust, Distributed, Dense Metric-Semantic SLAM for Multi-Robot Systems
summary: Distributed multi-robot SLAM where robots exchange compact information peer to peer and jointly optimize with outlier-robust distributed pose-graph optimization.
key_takeaways: Peer-to-peer, no central server
Robust to bad inter-robot loop closures

title: Event-based Vision: A Survey
summary: Comprehensive survey of event cameras: sensing principle, algorithms (feature tracking, optical flow, VO/SLAM) and applications.
key_takeaways: Microsecond latency and high dynamic range
Algorithms must be redesigned for asynchronous data

title: How NeRFs and 3D Gaussian Splatting are Reshaping SLAM: a Survey
summary: Survey of SLAM methods that use neural radiance fields or 3D Gaussian splatting as the map representation, organized by sensor and technique.
key_takeaways: Radiance-field maps trade compute for photorealism
Most methods are GPU-bound and not yet embedded-ready

title: Gaussian Splatting SLAM
summary: Monocular and RGB-D SLAM that tracks and maps directly against 3D Gaussians using analytic Jacobians for camera pose optimization.
key_takeaways: Single representation for tracking, mapping and rendering

title: LiDAR Odometry Survey: Recent Advancements and Remaining Challenges
summary: Survey of LiDAR-only, LiDAR-inertial and multi-sensor LiDAR odometry, with discussion of datasets, evaluation and open challenges such as degeneracy.
key_takeaways: Taxonomy of LiDAR, LiDAR-inertial and LiDAR-plus-other fusion
Geometric degeneracy (tunnels, open fields) is a key open issue

title: 4D Millimeter-Wave Radar in Autonomous Driving: A Survey
summary: Survey of 4D imaging radar: signal processing, datasets, calibration, perception and SLAM/odometry uses.
key_takeaways: 4D radar adds elevation and works in adverse weather
Sparse, noisy point clouds need radar-specific methods

title: CFEAR Radarodometry - Conservative Filtering for Efficient and Accurate Radar Odometry
summary: Learning-free spinning-radar odometry that keeps the strongest returns per azimuth, builds oriented surface points and registers against a keyframe history (IROS 2021).
key_takeaways: Simple filtering beats heavier radar pipelines
Runs fast on a single CPU thread per the authors

title: Edge-based Monocular Thermal-Inertial Odometry in Visually Degraded Environments
summary: Thermal-inertial odometry that tracks thermal image edges instead of corner features, targeting darkness and smoke where visible cameras fail.
key_takeaways: Thermal edges are more stable than corners in low-contrast IR
Relevant for night and obscurant operations

title: ArduPilot EKF3 source-set switch under GPS denial
summary: Flies ArduCopter SITL on GPS, switches EKF3 to an external-nav source set (SITL vicon) with MAV_CMD_SET_EKF_SOURCE_SET or an RC aux switch, cuts simulated GPS, keeps flying, then restores it. EKF_STATUS_REPORT is logged throughout, decoded by a stdlib module with unit tests.
verified: ekf_flags.py and test_ekf_flags.py ran with python3.14.7 stdlib on 2026-11-06 (6 tests OK), output shown in README. source_switch.py is an unverified sketch: syntax-checked only, requires pymavlink and ArduPilot SITL (sim_vehicle.py with the vicon simulator); parameter names were checked against ArduPilot master and the ArduPilot-4.6 branch source on 2026-11-06.

title: GNSS/INS EKF through a GNSS outage and a spoofing walk-off
summary: A stdlib-only 2D loosely-coupled GNSS/INS EKF (8 states, hand-written matrix helpers) on a synthetic vehicle with biased, noisy 100 Hz IMU and 1 Hz GNSS. It compares INS-only, EKF, EKF with a chi-square innovation gate, and a gated EKF that latches into holdover through a 60 s outage and a slowly walking spoofed offset. A sweep shows that the gate catches fast walk-offs but misses slow ones.
verified: ran with python3.14.7 stdlib on 2026-11-06 (default run and --sweep), output shown in README. Uses no third-party code; the referenced repos were not run.

title: GNSS interference monitor from u-blox telemetry and ADS-B NACp
summary: A stdlib heuristic scorer turns per-epoch receiver telemetry (C/N0 across SVs, AGC, CW jamming indicator, clock and position jumps, receiver spoofing/jamming flags) into jamming and spoofing scores with stated reasons. A pyubx2 adapter feeds it live from UBX NAV-SAT, NAV-STATUS, NAV-CLOCK, MON-RF and SEC-SIG. A second stdlib module applies the GPSJam percentage method to readsb aircraft.json NACp for area-level interference maps.
verified: scorer.py, adsb_area_map.py and their 14 unit tests ran with python3.14.7 stdlib on 2026-11-06, output shown in README; a negative control (cn0_drop weight 0) made test_broadband_jamming fail as expected. ubx_monitor.py is an unverified sketch: syntax-checked only, requires pyubx2 (attribute names checked against pyubx2 v1.4.1 ubxtypes_get.py) and a u-blox receiver; readsb field names were checked against its README-json.md.

title: Public CORS RINEX to SPP vs RTK with RTKLIB demo5 and gnss_lib_py
summary: Downloads one day of public NOAA NGS CORS RINEX for a rover/base pair 30 km apart, runs RTKLIB demo5 rnx2rtkp in single-point and kinematic RTK modes with exact CLI flags, and scores both against the stations' published ITRF2020 coordinates (propagated for plate motion) in ENU. An optional gnss_lib_py weighted-least-squares SPP covers the same data in Python, after converting RINEX 2.11 to 3.
verified: unverified sketch: syntax-checked only (bash -n, py_compile); requires RTKLIB demo5 rnx2rtkp/convbin, crx2rnx, and gnss-lib-py. rnx2rtkp/convbin flags were checked against demo5 v2.5.1 source help text and gnss_lib_py calls against v1.1.0 source on 2026-11-06. The stdlib scorer compare_pos.py and its 4 unit tests ran with python3.14.7 on 2026-11-06, and its coordinate parser ran on the real downloaded NGS sheets; the data URLs returned HTTP 200 and the P730 RINEX header was inspected. No RTKLIB or gnss_lib_py solution was computed.

title: Querying the hub from LLM agents via MCP
summary: A stdlib-only MCP stdio server (tools/mcp_server.py) exposes search, show, concept and neighbors over the hub's index and graph so Claude Code, Cursor and other MCP clients can query it as tools. The README covers client registration, a navigation path for agents (llms.txt, INDEX.md, concept pages, records.jsonl) and prompt recipes.
verified: tools/mcp_server.py ran with python3.14.7 stdlib on 2026-11-06 by piping demo_requests.jsonl into it (initialize, tools/list, tools/call for search/concept/neighbors/show, error paths); transcript shown in README. Client registration (Claude Code, Cursor, others) was not exercised.

title: MagNav.jl quickstart: Tolles-Lawson and EKF on the SGL 2020 flight
summary: A Julia walkthrough with MagNav.jl that downloads the public SGL 2020 challenge flight and Ottawa anomaly maps, compensates the scalar magnetometer with Tolles-Lawson on a calibration box, and runs the MagNav EKF against the map, printing INS-only vs EKF error and the CRLB. The README explains why magnetic anomaly navigation resists jamming and spoofing, and where it breaks down (map coverage, altitude, aircraft noise, temporal variation).
verified: unverified sketch: never run, Julia not installed; function names and signatures checked against MagNav.jl v1.3.5 examples and src on 2026-11-06; requires Julia 1.10+, MagNav.jl, CSV.jl, DataFrames.jl and the package's data artifacts.

title: MAVLink telemetry to TAK Cursor-on-Target
summary: Bridges autopilot GLOBAL_POSITION_INT messages into Cursor-on-Target events so a UAV shows up as a friendly track on ATAK, WinTAK or iTAK. A stdlib-only CoT builder with unit tests is paired with a pymavlink + PyTAK bridge that targets a TAK server or Mesh SA multicast.
verified: cot.py and test_cot.py ran with python3.14.7 stdlib on 2026-11-06 (4 tests OK), output shown in README; bridge.py is an unverified sketch: syntax-checked only, requires pymavlink and pytak plus a MAVLink source and TAK endpoint.

title: PX4 SITL GPS denial: inject, measure drift, recover
summary: Flies a square mission in PX4 SITL (Gazebo gz_x500), turns the GPS off mid-mission with MAVSDK failure injection, logs EKF2 health and estimated vs ground-truth position, then restores GPS and returns home. A stdlib analyzer reports per-phase horizontal drift and time to a 5 m error, and reads 'not measured' when no truth is available.
verified: drift.py and test_drift.py ran with python3.14.7 stdlib on 2026-11-06 (4 tests OK, synthetic drift output shown in README). gps_denial_mission.py and ulog_drift.py are unverified sketches: syntax-checked only, require mavsdk-grpc with PX4 SITL (Gazebo) and pyulog respectively.

title: Stone Soup radar tracking of two UAVs with JPDA and OSPA
summary: Simulates two small UAVs observed by a noisy bearing/range radar with clutter and tracks them with Stone Soup's Extended Kalman filter and JPDA data association. Track quality is scored against ground truth with the OSPA metric, the detect-and-track layer of a counter-UAS airspace picture.
verified: unverified sketch: syntax-checked only with python3.14.7 on 2026-11-06; requires stonesoup (numpy, scipy). Class names checked against Stone Soup tutorials 02, 08 and the Metrics example.

title: Terrain-relative navigation with a particle filter
summary: A stdlib-only simulation of TERCOM/TRN: an aircraft with a biased INS and a radar altimeter matches its measured terrain profile against a seeded synthetic DEM with a particle filter that also estimates the INS velocity bias. Prints INS-only vs PF error over time, includes a flat-terrain control, and a rasterio loader for Copernicus GLO-30 tiles.
verified: terrain.py and trn_pf.py ran with python3.14.7 stdlib on 2026-11-06, output shown in README; dem_rasterio.py is an unverified sketch: syntax-checked only, requires rasterio (the GLO-30 tile URL returned HTTP 200 on 2026-11-06).

title: VIO to MAVLink bridge with ENU/FLU to NED/FRD conversion
summary: Sends an external pose source (VIO topic or CSV log) to PX4 EKF2 or ArduPilot EKF3 as VISION_POSITION_ESTIMATE or ODOMETRY for GPS-denied position hold. The frame conversion (ENU/FLU to NED/FRD, world to body velocity, MAVLink covariance layout) is a stdlib module with unit tests, and the pymavlink sender is a thin sketch on top.
verified: frames.py and test_frames.py ran with python3.14.7 stdlib on 2026-11-06 (8 tests OK), and bridge.py --dry-run ran on example_pose_enu.csv; output shown in README. The pymavlink send path and the SITL parameter recipes are an unverified sketch: syntax-checked only, requires pymavlink and a PX4 or ArduPilot SITL.

title: Drone frame to orthophoto geolocalization with LightGlue
summary: Matches a nadir drone frame against a georeferenced satellite or orthophoto tile with SuperPoint + LightGlue, fits a MAGSAC homography with OpenCV, and maps the frame centre through the GeoTIFF geotransform to lat/lon. The geometry (affine geotransform, homography mapping, WGS84 UTM, haversine) is a stdlib module with unit tests; the pipeline points at UAV-VisLoc, VPAIR and University-1652 for imagery and at hloc / AnyLoc for retrieval over large maps.
verified: geo_math.py and test_geo_math.py ran with python3.14.7 stdlib on 2026-11-06 (12 tests OK), output shown in README; geolocalize.py is an unverified sketch: syntax-checked only, requires torch, lightglue, opencv-python, rasterio and numpy.
